```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import scipy.stats as sstat
from math import floor, log10

DOC = "PCR-004"
UO = "harvest"
UO_TITLE = "Harvest and Clarification (Step 4)"

# --- identity, versions, campaign constants ------------------------------------------------
VER, EFF = doc_version(DOC)
PLAN = "PCP-004"
V1_DATE = rev1_date(DOC)                 # Version 1.0 of this report
PLAN_V1 = rev1_date(PLAN)                # approval of PCP-004 Version 1.0, before the studies
SCALE_L = f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"
ALPHA = float(THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"])
NMC = int(V["n_monte_carlo"])
N_PPQ = int(V["n_ppq"])
assert CPK_TARGET > CPK_MIN


def n0(v):
    return T.num(v, 0)


def n1(v):
    return T.num(v, 1)


def n2(v):
    return T.num(v, 2)


def n3(v):
    return T.num(v, 3)


def gn(v):
    return f"{float(v):g}"


def cn(v):
    return f"{int(v):,}"


# --- parameters (names, units, ranges from the config) -------------------------------------
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
KEYS = ["centrifuge_g", "depth_filter_load", "turbidity"]
P = {k: uo.param(k) for k in KEYS}
N_PAR = len(uo.parameters)
assert N_PAR == len(KEYS) and all(P[k].study == "univariate" for k in KEYS)
# no NOR or set-point of this step changed at Version 2.0
assert all(list(P[k].nor) == list(P[k].nor_characterized) for k in KEYS)
assert all(P[k].setpoint_characterized is None or float(P[k].setpoint) == float(P[k].setpoint_characterized)
           for k in KEYS)
NAME = {k: P[k].name for k in KEYS}
LNAME = {k: NAME[k][0].lower() + NAME[k][1:] for k in KEYS}
UNIT = {k: P[k].unit for k in KEYS}
CLS = {k: P[k].classification for k in KEYS}
assert (CLS["centrifuge_g"], CLS["depth_filter_load"], CLS["turbidity"]) == ("KPP", "KPP", "GPP")
assert not any(CLS[k] in ("CPP", "WC-CPP") for k in KEYS)


def fg(v):
    """A setting as this report writes it: thousands separators, no trailing zero."""
    v = float(v)
    return f"{v:,.0f}" if abs(v) >= 1000 else f"{v:g}"


def pv(k, v):
    return f"{fg(v)} {P[k].unit}"


def pr(k, lo, hi):
    return f"{fg(lo)}–{fg(hi)} {P[k].unit}"


def sig3(v):
    """Three significant figures with thousands separators and a true minus (HCP, DNA)."""
    v = float(v)
    if v == 0:
        return "0"
    d = 2 - int(floor(log10(abs(v))))
    return T._minus(f"{round(v, d):,.{max(d, 0)}f}")


def n2h(v):
    """Two decimals, rounded half up on the decimal value (1.115 -> 1.12), for model values set in the config."""
    from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
    return str(Decimal(repr(round(float(v), 10))).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def fp(p):
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}"


def pp(p):
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"


SP_ = {k: pv(k, P[k].setpoint) for k in KEYS}
NOR_ = {k: pr(k, *P[k].nor) for k in KEYS}
RNG_ = {k: pr(k, *P[k].prange) for k in KEYS}
NORLO_ = {k: pv(k, P[k].nor[0]) for k in KEYS}
NORHI_ = {k: pv(k, P[k].nor[1]) for k in KEYS}
RLO_ = {k: pv(k, P[k].prange[0]) for k in KEYS}
RHI_ = {k: pv(k, P[k].prange[1]) for k in KEYS}
# the ranges studied extend beyond the NOR at both ends, except the lower end of turbidity
for k in ("centrifuge_g", "depth_filter_load"):
    assert P[k].prange[0] < P[k].nor[0] and P[k].prange[1] > P[k].nor[1]
assert P["turbidity"].prange[0] == P["turbidity"].nor[0] and P["turbidity"].prange[1] > P["turbidity"].nor[1]
CLAR_LIM = float(P["turbidity"].nor[1])  # PCP-004 §7 criterion 2: the upper limit of the NOR of turbidity
CLAR_ = pv("turbidity", CLAR_LIM)

# --- studies, chronology, registers ---------------------------------------------------------
CH = csv("study_chronology.csv").set_index("id")
UNI1 = "S-HAR-UNI"
UNI2 = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["univariate_nodoe"]["studies"][UO]
HLD = "S-HAR-HLD"
W = {s: (CH.loc[s, "start"], CH.loc[s, "end"]) for s in (UNI1, UNI2, HLD)}
WIN = {s: f"{W[s][0]} to {W[s][1]}" for s in W}
# the Version 2.0 studies were made after INV-001 closed and after AMD-001, and closed before this revision
for s in (UNI2, HLD):
    assert W[s][0] > INV["closed"] and W[s][0] > AMD["date"] and W[s][1] < EFF
assert PLAN_V1 < W[UNI1][0] < W[UNI1][1] < V1_DATE
assert W[UNI1][1] < AMD["date"]            # S-HAR-UNI closed before AMD-001
MP = csv("method_plan.csv").set_index("study")
assert not MP.loc[UNI1, "lmw_in_scope"]
assert MP.loc[UNI2, "lmw_cesds"] and MP.loc[HLD, "lmw_cesds"]
assert not MP.loc[UNI2, "lmw_sec"] and not MP.loc[HLD, "lmw_sec"]
PDS = {d["id"]: d for d in PLAN_DISCREPANCIES[DOC]}
assert sorted(PDS) == [f"PD-004-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, 9)]
_subj = {k: d["subject"].lower() for k, d in PDS.items()}
assert "samples before and after" in _subj["PD-004-04"] and "pressure" in _subj["PD-004-05"]
assert "centrate from the set-point" in _subj["PD-004-06"] and "records of execution" in _subj["PD-004-07"]
assert "rules the report states" in _subj["PD-004-08"]
assert "8,000 and 10,000 g" in PDS["PD-004-01"]["done"] and "fragments" in PDS["PD-004-01"]["done"]
assert "PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §5" in PDS["PD-004-02"]["done"]
assert PDS["PD-004-01"]["studies"] == [UNI2] and PDS["PD-004-02"]["studies"] == [HLD]
assert "not qualified" in PDS["PD-004-03"]["subject"]
N_PD = len(PDS)
EV = dev_facts(DOC)
assert list(EV["dev_id"]) == ["DEV-004-01", "DEV-004-02"] and set(EV["disposition"]) == {"retained"}
N_EV = len(EV)
assert dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu > CLAR_LIM                    # above the NOR
assert EV.set_index("dev_id").loc["DEV-004-01", "lot"] == "LOT-DF-4408"
assert EV.set_index("dev_id").loc["DEV-004-02", "method"] == "AMV-3015"
assert lot_df_4408_expiry > W[UNI1][1]                          # the lot was within its expiry
assert D.rev1_criteria(UO).empty                                # Version 1.0 applied no criterion here
assert D.iac_table(UO).empty                                    # PCMP-001 sets no IAC at harvest

# --- S-HAR-UNI2 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
UCFG = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["univariate_nodoe"]
U = csv("univariate_studies.csv")
U = U[U["study"] == UNI2].copy()
U["step_yield_pct"] = 100.0 * U["step_yield"]
NREP = int(UCFG["replicates"])
assert NREP == 2                                                 # "in duplicate"
NLEV = len(UCFG["levels"])
LEVNAMES = list(UCFG["levels"])
assert (U.groupby(["parameter", "level"]).size() == NREP).all()
assert sorted(U["parameter"].unique()) == sorted(KEYS)
N_RUNS = len(U)
N_SER = N_RUNS // len(KEYS)
LEV = {k: sorted(U.loc[U["parameter"] == k, "value"].unique()) for k in KEYS}
assert all(len(LEV[k]) == NLEV and LEV[k][0] == P[k].prange[0] and LEV[k][-1] == P[k].prange[1]
           and float(P[k].setpoint) in LEV[k] for k in KEYS)
# what the record of S-HAR-UNI2 does not hold (stated in the text)
assert U["harvest_hcp_ng_mg"].isna().all() and U["harvest_dna_pg_mg"].isna().all()   # no unclarified culture
assert U["aggregates_hmw"].isna().all()                                               # no aggregate before the step
assert not any("pressure" in c.lower() for c in U.columns)                           # no filter or column pressure
assert not any(("cycle" in c.lower()) or ("column" in c.lower()) for c in U.columns)  # no Protein A load challenge
assert not any(c.startswith("centrate_") and c != "centrate_turbidity_ntu" for c in U.columns)
assert not any("filtrate" in c.lower() for c in U.columns)
assert not any(("viab" in c.lower()) or ("vcd" in c.lower()) for c in U.columns)     # no culture viability
assert "run_order" not in U.columns
assert U.loc[U["parameter"] == "turbidity", "centrate_turbidity_ntu"].isna().all()
assert U["acidic_variants"].isna().all()                                             # acidic variants not measured
# every NOR lies between levels that were run
assert all(LEV[k][0] <= P[k].nor[0] and P[k].nor[1] <= LEV[k][-1] for k in KEYS)

RLAB = {"centrate_turbidity_ntu": "Centrate turbidity (NTU)",
        "clarified_turbidity_ntu": f"{NAME['turbidity']} ({P['turbidity'].unit})",
        "step_yield_pct": "Step yield (%)",
        "hcp_out_ng_mg": "Host cell protein (ng/mg)",
        "dna_out_pg_mg": "Residual DNA (pg/mg)",
        "aggregate_out_pct": T.ATTR_NAME["aggregates_hmw"],
        "lmw_cesds_pct": T.ATTR_NAME["fragments_lmw"]}
RORDER = list(RLAB)
ALAB = {"hcp": "Host cell protein", "residual_dna": "Residual DNA",
        "aggregates_hmw": T.ATTR_NAME["aggregates_hmw"].rsplit(" (", 1)[0],
        "fragments_lmw": T.ATTR_NAME["fragments_lmw"].rsplit(" (", 1)[0],
        "acidic_variants": T.ATTR_NAME["acidic_variants"].rsplit(" (", 1)[0]}
ATTRS = ["hcp_out_ng_mg", "dna_out_pg_mg", "aggregate_out_pct", "lmw_cesds_pct"]
ANAME = {"hcp_out_ng_mg": "host cell protein", "dna_out_pg_mg": "residual DNA",
         "aggregate_out_pct": "aggregate", "lmw_cesds_pct": "fragments", "step_yield_pct": "step yield"}
FMT = {"centrate_turbidity_ntu": T.num, "clarified_turbidity_ntu": T.num,
       "hcp_out_ng_mg": sig3, "dna_out_pg_mg": sig3,
       "aggregate_out_pct": n2, "lmw_cesds_pct": n2, "step_yield_pct": n1}
RUNIT = {"centrate_turbidity_ntu": "NTU", "clarified_turbidity_ntu": "NTU", "hcp_out_ng_mg": "ng/mg",
         "dna_out_pg_mg": "pg/mg", "aggregate_out_pct": "percentage points",
         "lmw_cesds_pct": "percentage points", "step_yield_pct": "percentage points"}

# the four runs at the full set-point condition (every parameter at its set-point, no adjustment)
SPR = U[(U["parameter"].isin(["centrifuge_g", "depth_filter_load"])) & (U["level"] == "set-point")]
N_SPR = len(SPR)


def regress(pk, rk):
    g = U[U["parameter"] == pk].dropna(subset=[rk])
    x, y = g["value"].to_numpy(float), g[rk].to_numpy(float)
    lr = sstat.linregress(x, y)
    n = len(x)
    tq = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, n - 2)
    res = y - (lr.intercept + lr.slope * x)
    rsd = float(np.sqrt((res ** 2).sum() / (n - 2)))
    w = float(P[pk].prange[1] - P[pk].prange[0])
    sxx = float(((x - x.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    # PCP-004 §5.5: the replicates at the set-point condition as the estimate of run-to-run variation
    s_sp = float(SPR[rk].std(ddof=1))
    df_sp = int(SPR[rk].notna().sum() - 1)
    se_sp = s_sp / np.sqrt(sxx)
    p_sp = float(2 * sstat.t.sf(abs(lr.slope / se_sp), df_sp))
    tq_sp = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, df_sp)
    nor_w = float(P[pk].nor[1] - P[pk].nor[0])
    return dict(pk=pk, rk=rk, n=n, slope=float(lr.slope), se=float(lr.stderr), icpt=float(lr.intercept),
                p=float(lr.pvalue), r2=float(lr.rvalue ** 2), rsd=rsd, chg=float(lr.slope * w),
                lo=float((lr.slope - tq * lr.stderr) * w), hi=float((lr.slope + tq * lr.stderr) * w),
                p_sp=p_sp, df_sp=df_sp, se_sp=float(se_sp),
                lo_sp=float((lr.slope - tq_sp * se_sp) * w), hi_sp=float((lr.slope + tq_sp * se_sp) * w),
                chg_nor=float(lr.slope * nor_w))


REG = {}
for pk in KEYS:
    for rk in RORDER:
        if U.loc[U["parameter"] == pk, rk].notna().any():
            REG[(pk, rk)] = regress(pk, rk)
CHECK = ("turbidity", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")      # the challenge level against its target: a check
N_TESTS = len(REG) - 1
N_PER = REG[("centrifuge_g", "hcp_out_ng_mg")]["n"]
# PCP-004 §5.4 and §5.5: the replicates at the set-point condition are the error every effect is tested
# against, so they decide; the residual error of the regression is a sensitivity
SIG = {k: r["p_sp"] < ALPHA for k, r in REG.items()}
SIG_RES = {k: r["p"] < ALPHA for k, r in REG.items()}
DF_RES = N_PER - 2
DF_SP = REG[("centrifuge_g", "hcp_out_ng_mg")]["df_sp"]
EFFECTS = sorted(k for k, s in SIG.items() if s and k != CHECK)
assert EFFECTS == sorted([("centrifuge_g", "centrate_turbidity_ntu"), ("centrifuge_g", "clarified_turbidity_ntu"),
                          ("depth_filter_load", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")])
assert SIG[CHECK] and REG[CHECK]["r2"] > 0.99
assert not any(SIG[(pk, rk)] for pk in KEYS for rk in ATTRS)            # no attribute slope
assert not any(SIG[(pk, "step_yield_pct")] for pk in KEYS)              # no step yield slope
assert not SIG[("depth_filter_load", "centrate_turbidity_ntu")]
assert SIG_RES == SIG                                                   # same decisions with the residual error
# directions stated in the text
assert REG[("centrifuge_g", "centrate_turbidity_ntu")]["chg"] < 0
assert REG[("centrifuge_g", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")]["chg"] < 0
assert REG[("depth_filter_load", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")]["chg"] > 0


def rr(pk, rk, what="chg"):
    return FMT[rk](REG[(pk, rk)][what])


def ci(pk, rk):
    r = REG[(pk, rk)]
    return f"{FMT[rk](r['lo_sp'])} to {FMT[rk](r['hi_sp'])}"


def ci_res(pk, rk):
    r = REG[(pk, rk)]
    return f"{FMT[rk](r['lo'])} to {FMT[rk](r['hi'])}"


def pR(pk, rk):
    return pp(REG[(pk, rk)]["p_sp"])


# level means and individual results
MEAN = {pk: U[U["parameter"] == pk].groupby("value")[RORDER].mean() for pk in KEYS}
lo_g, sp_g, hi_g = LEV["centrifuge_g"][0], float(P["centrifuge_g"].setpoint), LEV["centrifuge_g"][-1]
CEN = MEAN["centrifuge_g"]["centrate_turbidity_ntu"]
assert CEN.is_monotonic_decreasing
CEN_FALL = CEN[lo_g] - CEN[hi_g]
CEN1 = {v: round(float(CEN[v]), 1) for v in LEV["centrifuge_g"]}   # the level means as the clarification table prints them
CEN_FALL1 = CEN1[lo_g] - CEN1[hi_g]
CEN_FRAC = (CEN[lo_g] - CEN[sp_g]) / CEN_FALL
assert CEN_FRAC > 0.5                                                   # most of the fall below the set-point
CLM = MEAN["centrifuge_g"]["clarified_turbidity_ntu"]

# clarification criterion, individual results of the centrifugation (rcf) and depth filter load series
CLAR = {}
for pk in ("centrifuge_g", "depth_filter_load"):
    g = U[U["parameter"] == pk]
    CLAR[pk] = {v: g.loc[g["value"] == v, "clarified_turbidity_ntu"].to_numpy(float) for v in LEV[pk]}
PASS = {pk: {v: bool(np.all(CLAR[pk][v] <= CLAR_LIM)) for v in LEV[pk]} for pk in CLAR}
PASS["turbidity"] = {v: True for v in LEV["turbidity"]}   # criteria 1 and 3 by slope; criterion 2 not applicable
assert all(PASS["centrifuge_g"].values())
FAIL_DFL = [v for v in LEV["depth_filter_load"] if not PASS["depth_filter_load"][v]]
assert FAIL_DFL == [LEV["depth_filter_load"][-1]]
TOP_DFL = FAIL_DFL[0]
TOPR = np.sort(CLAR["depth_filter_load"][TOP_DFL])
assert np.all(TOPR > CLAR_LIM)                                          # both results above the limit
PREV_DFL = LEV["depth_filter_load"][-2]
PREVR = np.sort(CLAR["depth_filter_load"][PREV_DFL])
LOW3_DFL = [v for v in LEV["depth_filter_load"] if v < PREV_DFL]
low3 = np.concatenate([CLAR["depth_filter_load"][v] for v in LOW3_DFL])
assert np.all(PREVR > low3.max())                                       # both at the next level above every lower result
assert np.all(PREVR < CLAR_LIM)
DFL_LOW_RANGE = (low3.min(), low3.max())
MAX_CLAR_RCF = max(CLAR["centrifuge_g"][v].max() for v in LEV["centrifuge_g"])
MAX_CLAR_RCF_AT = [v for v in LEV["centrifuge_g"] if CLAR["centrifuge_g"][v].max() == MAX_CLAR_RCF][0]
DFL_TOP_RATIO = MEAN["depth_filter_load"].loc[TOP_DFL, "clarified_turbidity_ntu"] / \
    MEAN["depth_filter_load"].loc[PREV_DFL, "clarified_turbidity_ntu"]
assert DFL_TOP_RATIO > 2                                                 # "more than doubled"


def par_of(pk):
    lv, sp = LEV[pk], float(P[pk].setpoint)
    i = lv.index(sp)
    assert PASS[pk][sp]
    a = i
    while a - 1 >= 0 and PASS[pk][lv[a - 1]]:
        a -= 1
    b = i
    while b + 1 < len(lv) and PASS[pk][lv[b + 1]]:
        b += 1
    return lv[a], lv[b]


PAR = {k: par_of(k) for k in KEYS}
PAR_ = {k: pr(k, *PAR[k]) for k in KEYS}
PARCHG_CEN = float(CEN[PAR["centrifuge_g"][1]] - CEN[PAR["centrifuge_g"][0]])
PARCHG_CEN1 = CEN1[PAR["centrifuge_g"][1]] - CEN1[PAR["centrifuge_g"][0]]
PARCHG_CRCF = float(CLM[PAR["centrifuge_g"][1]] - CLM[PAR["centrifuge_g"][0]])
PARCHG_CDFL = float(MEAN["depth_filter_load"].loc[PAR["depth_filter_load"][1], "clarified_turbidity_ntu"]
                    - MEAN["depth_filter_load"].loc[PAR["depth_filter_load"][0], "clarified_turbidity_ntu"])
assert PARCHG_CEN < 0 and PARCHG_CRCF < 0 and PARCHG_CDFL > 0
assert PAR["centrifuge_g"] == tuple(P["centrifuge_g"].prange)
assert PAR["turbidity"] == tuple(P["turbidity"].prange)
assert PAR["depth_filter_load"] == (P["depth_filter_load"].prange[0], PREV_DFL)
MARG = {k: (P[k].nor[0] - PAR[k][0], PAR[k][1] - P[k].nor[1]) for k in KEYS}
assert all(m[0] >= 0 and m[1] >= 0 for m in MARG.values())             # each NOR inside its PAR
assert MARG["depth_filter_load"][1] == 0 and MARG["turbidity"][0] == 0   # the two edges that coincide
assert MARG["centrifuge_g"][0] == MARG["centrifuge_g"][1] > 0
assert MARG["depth_filter_load"][0] > 0 and MARG["turbidity"][1] > 0

# plan levels (PCP-004 Appendix A) against the levels run
PLAN_LEV = {k: [P[k].prange[0], P[k].nor[0], float(P[k].setpoint), P[k].nor[1], P[k].prange[1]] for k in KEYS}
NOT_RUN = {k: sorted({float(v) for v in PLAN_LEV[k]} - {float(v) for v in LEV[k]}) for k in KEYS}
assert NOT_RUN["depth_filter_load"] == []
assert NOT_RUN["centrifuge_g"] == [float(P["centrifuge_g"].nor[0]), float(P["centrifuge_g"].nor[1])]
assert NOT_RUN["turbidity"] == [float(P["turbidity"].nor[1])]
EXTRA = {k: sorted({float(v) for v in LEV[k]} - {float(v) for v in PLAN_LEV[k]}) for k in KEYS}
_nr = [pv(k, v) for k in KEYS for v in NOT_RUN[k]]
assert len(_nr) == 3
NOTRUN_WORD = "Three"
NOTRUN_TXT = join_and(_nr)
assert len(EXTRA["centrifuge_g"]) == 2 and len(EXTRA["turbidity"]) == 2
# the inner levels of centrifugation (rcf) lie outside its NOR
assert all(v < P["centrifuge_g"].nor[0] or v > P["centrifuge_g"].nor[1] for v in EXTRA["centrifuge_g"])

# the challenge: the measured level against its target
TURB_MEAS = (U.loc[U["parameter"] == "turbidity", "clarified_turbidity_ntu"].min(),
             U.loc[U["parameter"] == "turbidity", "clarified_turbidity_ntu"].max())

# precision of the runs: set-point runs and pooled duplicates, against the method records
METH = {m["id"]: m for m in CFG.raw()["deviations"]["methods"]}
METH_OF = {"centrate_turbidity_ntu": "AMV-3015", "clarified_turbidity_ntu": "AMV-3015",
           "hcp_out_ng_mg": "AMV-3012", "dna_out_pg_mg": "AMV-3014"}


def pooled_rsd(rk):
    d = U.dropna(subset=[rk])
    g = d.groupby(["parameter", "value"])[rk]
    ss = float(g.agg(lambda v: ((v - v.mean()) ** 2).sum()).sum())
    df = len(d) - g.ngroups
    return 100.0 * np.sqrt(ss / df) / d[rk].mean(), df


POOL = {rk: pooled_rsd(rk) for rk in RORDER}
SPSTAT = {rk: (SPR[rk].mean(), SPR[rk].std(ddof=1)) for rk in RORDER}
ASSAY_SHARE = {rk: (METH[METH_OF[rk]]["precision_pct"] / POOL[rk][0]) ** 2
               for rk in ("clarified_turbidity_ntu", "hcp_out_ng_mg", "dna_out_pg_mg")}
assert all(v > 0.5 for v in ASSAY_SHARE.values())    # assay variation is most of the duplicate scatter
SPCV = {rk: 100 * SPSTAT[rk][1] / SPSTAT[rk][0] for rk in RORDER}
assert SPCV["dna_out_pg_mg"] == max(SPCV.values())
DNA_SPR = (SPR["dna_out_pg_mg"].min(), SPR["dna_out_pg_mg"].max())
# the methods of aggregate and fragments: SEC validated under AMV-3011 (SOP-3011), its qualified performance
# recorded under AMV-3221 (the corpus convention); nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020, SOP-3015) with an absolute repeatability
SECM = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["sec"]
CESDS = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["cesds"]
SEC_Q = METH["AMV-3221"]
assert SECM["id"] == "AMV-3011" and SECM["sop"] == "SOP-3011"
assert CESDS["id"] == "AMV-3020" and CESDS["sop"] == "SOP-3015"
FRAG_MEAN = float(U["lmw_cesds_pct"].mean())
FRAG_POOL_SD = POOL["lmw_cesds_pct"][0] / 100 * FRAG_MEAN
METH_PREC = {"centrate_turbidity_ntu": METH["AMV-3015"]["precision_pct"],
             "clarified_turbidity_ntu": METH["AMV-3015"]["precision_pct"],
             "hcp_out_ng_mg": METH["AMV-3012"]["precision_pct"], "dna_out_pg_mg": METH["AMV-3014"]["precision_pct"],
             "aggregate_out_pct": SEC_Q["precision_pct"], "lmw_cesds_pct": 100 * CESDS["sd_abs"] / FRAG_MEAN}
# "scatter at about the precision of the method": the pooled duplicates within a quarter to a third of it
assert all(0.75 < POOL[rk][0] / METH_PREC[rk] < 1.33 for rk in METH_PREC)
# practical significance as PCP-004 §5.5 defines it: each significant slope's change across the NOR against the
# precision of its method. The repeatability limit of a method is the difference two single results exceed by
# chance with a probability of 5 %, 1.96 x sqrt(2) times the SD of a single result at the set-point mean
# (the report's rule, PD-004-08)
Z_RES = float(sstat.norm.ppf(0.975) * np.sqrt(2))
PRACT = {}
for _k in EFFECTS:
    _sd1 = METH_PREC[_k[1]] / 100 * SPSTAT[_k[1]][0]
    PRACT[_k] = dict(chg=REG[_k]["chg_nor"], sd=_sd1, res=Z_RES * _sd1, material=abs(REG[_k]["chg_nor"]) >= Z_RES * _sd1)
PS_CEN = PRACT[("centrifuge_g", "centrate_turbidity_ntu")]
PS_CRCF = PRACT[("centrifuge_g", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")]
PS_CDFL = PRACT[("depth_filter_load", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")]
assert PS_CEN["material"] and not PS_CRCF["material"] and PS_CDFL["material"]
assert abs(TOPR[1] - TOPR[0]) < PS_CDFL["res"]                       # the two failing results agree
DFL_NOR_MEAN_CHG = float(MEAN["depth_filter_load"].loc[P["depth_filter_load"].nor[1], "clarified_turbidity_ntu"]
                         - MEAN["depth_filter_load"].loc[P["depth_filter_load"].nor[0], "clarified_turbidity_ntu"])
assert 0 < DFL_NOR_MEAN_CHG < PS_CDFL["chg"] and DFL_NOR_MEAN_CHG >= PS_CDFL["res"]
# results above the limit of quantitation of turbidity, HCP and DNA
for rk in METH_OF:
    assert U[rk].dropna().min() > METH[METH_OF[rk]]["loq"]

# attribute bands and the precision of the comparisons
BAND = {rk: (U[rk].min(), U[rk].max()) for rk in ATTRS + ["step_yield_pct"]}
CI_REL = {rk: 100 * max(max(abs(REG[(pk, rk)]["lo_sp"]), abs(REG[(pk, rk)]["hi_sp"])) for pk in KEYS) / SPSTAT[rk][0]
          for rk in ATTRS}
CI_REL_RES = {rk: 100 * max(max(abs(REG[(pk, rk)]["lo"]), abs(REG[(pk, rk)]["hi"])) for pk in KEYS) / SPSTAT[rk][0]
              for rk in ATTRS}
assert all(CI_REL[rk] > CI_REL_RES[rk] for rk in ATTRS)                 # the plan's error gives the wider intervals
assert max(CI_REL, key=CI_REL.get) == "dna_out_pg_mg"
assert max(POOL, key=lambda r: POOL[r][0]) == "dna_out_pg_mg"
assert METH["AMV-3014"]["precision_pct"] == max(METH[m]["precision_pct"] for m in set(METH_OF.values()))
YIELD_SP = float(SPSTAT["step_yield_pct"][0])
CLOSEST = {pk: min(ATTRS, key=lambda rk: REG[(pk, rk)]["p_sp"]) for pk in KEYS}
assert CLOSEST["centrifuge_g"] == "hcp_out_ng_mg" and REG[("centrifuge_g", "hcp_out_ng_mg")]["chg"] < 0
assert REG[("turbidity", "step_yield_pct")]["p_sp"] == min(REG[("turbidity", r)]["p_sp"] for r in ATTRS + ["step_yield_pct"])

# --- criteria that pass through harvest (production bioreactor output, PCMP-001 Table 7.1) -------
IAC_B = D.iac_table("bioreactor").set_index("response")
AGG_C = D.ipc_limit("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw")
ACID_C = D.ipc_limit("bioreactor", "acidic_variants")
FRAG_DS = D.acceptance_for(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct")
assert AGG_C[2] == "upper" and ACID_C[2] == "two_sided" and FRAG_DS[2] == "upper"
assert D.ipc_limit(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct") is None and "lmw_cesds_pct" not in IAC_B.index
_fr = D.iac_table()
_fr = _fr[_fr["cqa"] == "fragments_lmw"]
assert np.isclose(_fr["iac_high"].min(), FRAG_DS[1])                     # no fragments criterion is stricter
agg_row = IAC_B.loc["aggregates_hmw"]
assert bool(agg_row["tightened"]) and bool(agg_row["widened"]) and agg_row["iac_high"] < agg_row["iac_high_apriori"]
acid_row = IAC_B.loc["acidic_variants"]
assert not bool(acid_row["tightened"]) and not bool(acid_row["widened"])
AGG_DS = D.acceptance_for("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw")[1]
# the aggregate criterion carried back through the three verified worst cases (PCMP-001 §7.5), at
# manufacturing scale: UF/DF increase, cation exchange clearance, low-pH viral inactivation increase
_iv = D.iac_verification().set_index(["step_key", "cqa"])
AGG_UFDF = _iv.loc[("ufdf", "aggregates_hmw")]
AGG_CEX = _iv.loc[("cex", "aggregates_hmw")]
AGG_VI = _iv.loc[("viral_inactivation", "aggregates_hmw")]
assert not bool(AGG_UFDF["met"]) and not bool(AGG_CEX["met"]) and bool(AGG_VI["widening_supported"])
assert np.isclose(AGG_CEX["predicted_nor_bound95"], agg_row["downstream_fold"], rtol=1e-3)   # the CSV keeps 4 decimals
assert np.isclose((AGG_DS - AGG_UFDF["predicted_nor_bound95"]) * AGG_CEX["predicted_nor_bound95"]
                  - AGG_VI["predicted_nor_bound95"], agg_row["iac_high"], rtol=1e-3)
assert np.isclose(AGG_UFDF["predicted_nor_bound95"] + AGG_VI["predicted_nor_bound95"], agg_row["downstream_added"], rtol=1e-3)
ACID_DS = D.acceptance_for("bioreactor", "acidic_variants")
assert BAND["aggregate_out_pct"][1] < AGG_C[1] and BAND["lmw_cesds_pct"][1] < FRAG_DS[1]
AGG_C_ = f"≤ {n2(AGG_C[1])} %"
ACID_C_ = f"{n1(ACID_C[0])}–{n1(ACID_C[1])} %"
FRAG_C_ = f"≤ {FRAG_DS[1]:g} %"

# --- the hold study S-HAR-HLD -----------------------------------------------------------------
H = csv("hold_harvest.csv")
TEMPS = list(dict.fromkeys(H["temperature"]))
assert len(TEMPS) == 2
COLD, WARM = TEMPS[0], TEMPS[1]
DAYS = [int(d) for d in sorted(H["day"].unique())]
HOLD_D = max(DAYS)
HCOL = {"hmw_pct": "aggregate", "lmw_cesds_pct": "fragments", "acidic_pct": "acidic variants"}


def hchg(col, temp):
    g = H[H["temperature"] == temp].sort_values("day")
    d0 = float(g.loc[g["day"] == 0, col].iloc[0])
    ch = g[col].to_numpy(float) - d0
    return dict(d0=d0, inc=float(ch.max()), inc_day=int(g["day"].iloc[int(ch.argmax())]),
                dec=float(ch.min()), dec_day=int(g["day"].iloc[int(ch.argmin())]), end=float(ch[-1]),
                vals=g[col].to_numpy(float))


HC = {(c, t): hchg(c, t) for c in HCOL for t in TEMPS}
H_D0_AGG = sorted(HC[("hmw_pct", t)]["d0"] for t in TEMPS)
assert max(H_D0_AGG) < SPR["aggregate_out_pct"].min()      # the held pool entered below every set-point run
D0DIFF = {c: abs(HC[(c, COLD)]["d0"] - HC[(c, WARM)]["d0"]) for c in HCOL}
# warm hold: fragments rose at every time point; every attribute highest on the last day
assert np.all(np.diff(HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", WARM)]["vals"]) > 0)
assert all(HC[(c, WARM)]["end"] > 0 and HC[(c, WARM)]["end"] == HC[(c, WARM)]["inc"] for c in HCOL)
assert all(HC[(c, WARM)]["inc"] > HC[(c, COLD)]["inc"] for c in HCOL)
# most of the warm rise in acidic variants came after day 1
assert HC[("acidic_pct", WARM)]["vals"][1] <= HC[("acidic_pct", WARM)]["vals"][0]
# cold hold: aggregate back near day 0 on the last day; acidic variants within the precision of icIEF
ICIEF_SD = METH["AMV-3013"]["precision_pct"] / 100 * HC[("acidic_pct", COLD)]["d0"]
ACID_COLD_MAX = max(abs(HC[("acidic_pct", COLD)]["inc"]), abs(HC[("acidic_pct", COLD)]["dec"]))
assert ACID_COLD_MAX < ICIEF_SD
assert abs(HC[("hmw_pct", COLD)]["end"]) < D0DIFF["hmw_pct"]
fc = HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", COLD)]
assert fc["inc_day"] == 1 and fc["vals"][-1] <= fc["vals"][1] and fc["inc"] > D0DIFF["lmw_cesds_pct"]
assert fc["end"] > D0DIFF["lmw_cesds_pct"]
# the change over the hold is the largest change from day 0, here as in the judgement of the held pool
WARM_COLD_FRAG = HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", WARM)]["inc"] / HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", COLD)]["inc"]
assert WARM_COLD_FRAG > 1

ENTER = {("hmw_pct", "upper"): D.nor_prediction_limit("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw", "upper"),
         ("acidic_pct", "upper"): D.nor_prediction_limit("bioreactor", "acidic_variants", "upper"),
         ("acidic_pct", "lower"): D.nor_prediction_limit("bioreactor", "acidic_variants", "lower"),
         ("lmw_cesds_pct", "upper"): float(U["lmw_cesds_pct"].max())}
HCRIT = {"hmw_pct": AGG_C, "acidic_pct": ACID_C, "lmw_cesds_pct": FRAG_DS}
HJ = {}
for (c, side), e in ENTER.items():
    lo, hi, _ = HCRIT[c]
    for t in TEMPS:
        chg = HC[(c, t)]["inc"] if side == "upper" else min(HC[(c, t)]["dec"], 0.0)
        after = e + chg
        HJ[(c, side, t)] = dict(enter=e, chg=chg, after=after,
                                met=bool(after <= hi) if side == "upper" else bool(after >= lo))
assert all(HJ[(c, "upper", t)]["met"] for c in HCOL for t in TEMPS)
assert not any(HJ[("acidic_pct", "lower", t)]["met"] for t in TEMPS)
assert ENTER[("acidic_pct", "lower")] < ACID_C[0]                        # not met at entry already
HF = HJ[("lmw_cesds_pct", "upper", WARM)]
HA = HJ[("hmw_pct", "upper", WARM)]
HAU = HJ[("acidic_pct", "upper", WARM)]

# --- capability (integrated model, PCMP-001 §6.5) ---------------------------------------------
CAPK = ["fragments_lmw", "hcp", "residual_dna", "aggregates_hmw"]
CAPT = cap.set_index("key")
MC = csv("monte_carlo.csv")
POOS = D.p_oos().set_index("key")
assert all(CAPT.loc[k, "Cpk"] >= CPK_TARGET for k in CAPK)
assert all(int(POOS.loc[k, "n_oos"]) == 0 for k in CAPK)
N_MC = int(POOS.loc["fragments_lmw", "n"])
assert N_MC == NMC == len(MC)
UB0 = 1 - 0.05 ** (1 / N_MC)                    # one-sided 95 % upper bound with none of N outside
FRAG_NOM = V["fragments_nominal"]
FRAG_SP = float(SPR["lmw_cesds_pct"].mean())
FRAG_HOLD_DAYS = (FRAG_NOM["harvest"] - FRAG_NOM["bioreactor"]) / CFG.raw()["analytics"]["fragments"]["harvest_hold_rate_2_8"]
assert np.isclose(FRAG_HOLD_DAYS, 1.0)                     # the process model holds the harvest one day at 2-8 °C
assert abs(FRAG_NOM["bioreactor"] - FRAG_SP) < SPSTAT["lmw_cesds_pct"][1]   # end of culture against the runs
assert D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR == 6.0                              # "one sixth of the width of its NOR"
assert abs(FRAG_NOM["harvest"] - FRAG_SP) < SPSTAT["lmw_cesds_pct"][1]     # "agrees": within the set-point SD
CPK_FRAG = float(CAPT.loc["fragments_lmw", "Cpk"])
MC_FRAG = float(MC["fragments_lmw"].mean())
# residual DNA per dose at the clarified harvest, and the clearance the model credits downstream
DOSE_KG, DOSE_MGKG = DOSE["body_weight_kg"], DOSE["mg_per_kg"]
DNA_SP = float(SPSTAT["dna_out_pg_mg"][0])
DNA_DOSE = dna_ng_per_dose(DNA_SP)
DNA_DS = float(D.acceptance_for("bioreactor", "residual_dna")[1])
DNA_LOG_NEEDED = log10(DNA_DOSE / DNA_DS)
DNA_LRV = {k: CFG.raw()["process"][k].get("model", {}).get("dna_lrv") for k in CFG.train_order}
DNA_LRV = {k: float(v) for k, v in DNA_LRV.items() if v is not None}
assert sorted(DNA_LRV) == ["aex", "cex", "protein_a"]
assert sum(DNA_LRV.values()) > DNA_LOG_NEEDED
DNA_MARGIN = sum(DNA_LRV.values()) - DNA_LOG_NEEDED                # log10 of clearance credited beyond the need

# --- risk mitigation of PCR-003 executed at harvest -------------------------------------------
AM = D.acidic_mitigation()

# --- figure style ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C1, C2, INK2, NORC, GRID = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#52514e", "#e9e8e4", "#dddcd7"
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

This report presents the process characterization of harvest and clarification, Step 4 of the A-Mab drug substance process, at Version `{python} VER`. The study was planned in PCP-004. At commercial scale the step clarifies the contents of a `{python} SCALE_L` L production bioreactor by continuous disk-stack centrifugation, depth filtration and sterilizing-grade filtration, and it delivers the clarified harvest to Protein A capture. The A-Mab case study assumes, for simplicity, that harvest has no impact on product quality [@amab2009]. The drug substance CQA register nevertheless assigns fragments to this step, because proteases from lysed cells continue to clip the antibody while the clarified harvest is held. The report supports the transfer of the process from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION` to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`.

Version 1.0 of this report described a univariate study of each parameter, S-HAR-UNI (`{python} WIN[UNI1]`), and narrated its outcome without a result for any parameter effect. That study has no data in the record. During the Version 2.0 re-analysis, after the QA investigation INV-001 closed, two further studies were made. In the univariate study S-HAR-UNI2 (`{python} WIN[UNI2]`) each parameter was run at `{python} NLEV` levels in duplicate, with the other parameters at their set-points. In the hold study S-HAR-HLD (`{python} WIN[HLD]`) one pool of clarified harvest was held at two temperatures for `{python} HOLD_D` days. PCP-004 foresaw neither study, and each is recorded as a discrepancy from the plan (PD-004-01 and PD-004-02). The scale-down model of the harvest train was not qualified, because no laboratory-scale disk-stack centrifuge exists (PD-004-03). Every result is therefore stated at the scale of the study, and its offset from manufacturing scale is unknown, not zero. Five further discrepancies record what the study did not do as the plan set out. The culture and the centrate were not sampled, the filter pressure and the Protein A load challenge were not measured, the depth filter load series was run only on centrate from the set-point field, records of execution were not kept, and this report states the rules the plan leaves open (PD-004-04 to PD-004-08).

Turbidity responded to the parameters, and no effect on a quality attribute was detected. Centrate turbidity fell from a mean of `{python} n1(CEN[lo_g])` NTU at `{python} RLO_["centrifuge_g"]` to `{python} n1(CEN[hi_g])` NTU at `{python} RHI_["centrifuge_g"]`. Post-clarification turbidity stayed at or below `{python} n2(max(MAX_CLAR_RCF, PREVR.max()))` NTU across the whole range of centrifugation (rcf) and across depth filter load up to `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", PREV_DFL)`. Both runs at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)` exceeded the clarification limit of `{python} CLAR_`. Across the NOR of centrifugation (rcf) the change in post-clarification turbidity, `{python} n2(PS_CRCF["chg"])` NTU, is smaller than the repeatability limit of the turbidity method, the smallest difference between two single results that the method tells apart. No slope against the setting was detected for host cell protein, residual DNA, aggregate, fragments or step yield in any of the three series, at α = `{python} ALPHA`. The A-Mab assumption is therefore kept. The study supports it for the parameters, the ranges and the attributes it measured, and it did not measure the culture before harvest.

The proven acceptable range of centrifugation (rcf) is the whole range studied, `{python} PAR_["centrifuge_g"]`, with `{python} pv("centrifuge_g", MARG["centrifuge_g"][0])` of margin at each end of its NOR. The proven acceptable range of depth filter load is `{python} PAR_["depth_filter_load"]`, bounded by the clarification limit. The upper limit of its NOR lies on that edge, so the range leaves no margin above the NOR. The proven acceptable range of post-clarification turbidity, which is measured and not set, is `{python} PAR_["turbidity"]` for the attributes measured in the clarified harvest. It does not cover the performance of Protein A capture, and a harvest setting must still deliver turbidity within the NOR of `{python} NOR_["turbidity"]` (@sec-par). Centrifugation (rcf) and depth filter load were classified as KPPs, because each changed the clarity of the feed to capture and no effect of either on a quality attribute was detected. Post-clarification turbidity was classified as a GPP. No parameter of the step is a CPP or a WC-CPP.

At `{python} WARM` the held clarified harvest gained `{python} n2(HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", WARM)]["end"])` percentage points of fragments, `{python} n2(HC[("acidic_pct", WARM)]["end"])` of acidic variants and `{python} n2(HC[("hmw_pct", WARM)]["end"])` of aggregate in `{python} HOLD_D` days. At `{python} COLD` the changes were smaller. The held pool was judged against the criteria for the load of Protein A capture. For each attribute the highest level expected to enter the hold was added to the largest change from day `{python} DAYS[0]`, by rules this report chose after the results were known (@sec-stats). Aggregate, fragments and the upper limit for acidic variants met their criteria. The lowest level of acidic variants expected to enter the hold already lies below the lower limit, and PCR-003 reports that result with the acceptance of its risk.

In a Monte Carlo simulation of the whole train through the step models, the drug substance Cpk for fragments is `{python} n2(CPK_FRAG)`, above the target of `{python} CPK_TARGET` set in PCMP-001. Version 1.0 recorded two study events in S-HAR-UNI, a depth filter flush turbidity above its alert limit (DEV-004-01) and a post-clarification turbidity above the NOR on one run (DEV-004-02). That study has no data in the record, so neither event bears on this report.

# Introduction {#sec-introduction}

## Product and unit operation {#sec-product}

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody developed on the platform of `{python} COMPANY` [@amab2009]. Its drug substance is produced in a fed-batch production bioreactor and purified by the platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, virus filtration and UF/DF.

Harvest and clarification, Step 4, lies between the production bioreactor and Protein A capture. At commercial scale it is run once per batch on the contents of a `{python} SCALE_L` L production bioreactor. The culture passes a continuous disk-stack centrifuge, a train of depth filters and a sterilizing-grade filter, in that order (SOP-2005 and SOP-2006). The clarified harvest is then held until capture.

The step removes cells and cell debris. It is not credited with clearing any impurity, and no viral clearance is claimed for it. Its settings change the feed to Protein A capture in two ways. A clarification that removes fewer cells and less debris passes more fine material to capture. An operation that breaks more cells releases more host cell protein and DNA into the clarified harvest.

The drug substance CQA register assigns fragments to this step (PCMP-001 Table 3.1). Proteases released by dead and lysing cells clip the antibody in the reactor, and clipping continues in the clarified harvest, because clarification removes the cells but not the proteases already in solution. PCMP-001 sets no criterion for fragments at harvest, and fragments are judged at the downstream steps (PCMP-001 Table 7.1).

## Objectives {#sec-objectives}

PCP-004 §2 set five objectives for the study, given here in its numbering:

1. Qualify a scale-down model of the commercial harvest train and show that it represents the centrifugation and depth filtration performance of that train.
2. Establish the effect of the centrifugal field, over `{python} RNG_["centrifuge_g"]`, on the clarity of the centrate and on the host cell protein and DNA released by cell breakage.
3. Establish the effect of depth filter load, over `{python} RNG_["depth_filter_load"]`, on the particulate content of the clarified harvest and on the pressure the filter train develops.
4. Establish whether the step alters the size-variant profile of the antibody, and establish the effect of post-clarification turbidity, over `{python} RNG_["turbidity"]`, on the material presented to capture.
5. Define a proven acceptable range for each parameter, determine whether the normal operating range lies inside the proven acceptable range, and provide the evidence on which each parameter is classified under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001.

Objective 1, the qualification of the scale-down model, was not met, because no qualification was made (@sec-sdm). Objective 2, the effect of the field, was met in part. The effect of the field on the clarity of the centrate was established, and no effect on host cell protein or DNA in the clarified harvest was detected (@sec-res-rcf). The release by cell breakage itself was not established, because the culture before harvest was not sampled (PD-004-04). Objective 3, the effect of depth filter load, was met for the particulate content of the clarified harvest and not for the filter pressure, which was not measured (PD-004-05). Objective 4, whether the step alters the size variants and how turbidity affects the material presented to capture, was met in part. The study shows whether a parameter changed aggregate or fragments in the clarified harvest, but it did not measure the antibody before the step, and the Protein A load challenge that was to show the effect of turbidity on capture was not run (@sec-univariate). Objective 5, the proven acceptable ranges and the evidence for the classes, was met within the limits stated in @sec-par.

## Regulatory and scientific basis {#sec-regulatory}

The study is part of the Stage 1 process design record of the commercial process [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) and ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11], with quality risk management under ICH Q9 [@ichq9]. Criticality is treated as a continuum, as ICH Q8(R2) describes [@ichq8]. A proven acceptable range is the range of a parameter over which the step has been shown to meet its criteria, with the other parameters held at their set-points [@ichq8].

The A-Mab case study supplies the CQA framework, the risk methodology and the assumption that harvest has no impact on product quality [@amab2009]. The case study notes that the assumption might not hold in a real process. No viral clearance is claimed for this step, and no spiking study was made [@ichq5a].

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge {#sec-platform}

Harvest by continuous centrifugation and depth filtration is the platform recovery operation at `{python} COMPANY`. It was used for three earlier antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and the equipment, the grade of the filter media and the control scheme are unchanged for A-Mab (PCP-004 §4.1). The mechanisms below are therefore expected to hold for A-Mab. They give the direction in which each parameter is expected to act, and the size of each effect for A-Mab is what this study measured.

In the disk-stack centrifuge, cells and debris settle under the centrifugal field at a velocity that rises with the field and with the difference between their density and that of the medium. A particle settles onto a disc, is captured there and slides outward to the bowl wall, from which the solids are discharged at intervals. A higher field therefore clarifies more completely. It can also break more cells. The culture is accelerated to the speed of the bowl in the feed zone, and the shear there rises with that speed, while the flow between the discs is laminar and low in shear. Cells broken in the feed zone release host cell protein and DNA into the centrate, and they leave fine debris that is harder to capture.

The depth filter train removes the fine debris and the colloidal material that the centrifuge passes. Its media are positively charged, so they adsorb part of the DNA and fine debris as well as retaining particles by size. A depth filter has a finite capacity. As retained solids fill the void space of the matrix and occupy its charged sites, the pressure drop rises and more fine material passes. At the extreme, cells and debris are forced through the pores. Depth filter load is the volume of centrate per unit of media area, and the solids that this volume carries decide how far the media are saturated.

Post-clarification turbidity measures the fine particulate and colloidal material that the filters passed. It is not set but produced by the other two parameters. A higher centrifugal field lowers it, because fewer cells and less debris reach the filters, and it can also raise it, because more broken cells leave fine debris. It rises as the filter load approaches the capacity of the media. It matters because this material reaches the Protein A column, where it fouls the bed and shortens the working life of the resin.

Host cell protein and DNA in the clarified harvest are the burden of the culture plus whatever cells release when they break during the operation. Harvest does not clear host cell protein. A gentle harvest keeps the burden close to what left the reactor, and a harsh one adds intracellular protein to it. Aggregate could rise at harvest only where the antibody meets an air-liquid interface strong enough to unfold it, in the feed zone or in a foaming transfer. Within normal operation that exposure is brief, so aggregate is not expected to change.

Fragments are clipped antibody, mostly cleaved in or near the hinge into Fab and Fab+Fc species. Clipping starts in the reactor, where proteases released by dead and lysing cells act on the secreted antibody. It continues in the clarified harvest, and its rate rises with temperature, so a harvest held cold clips more slowly than one held at room temperature. Fragments can also form by disulfide reduction. Lysed cells release reducing enzymes, thioredoxin reductase among them, which can break the interchain disulfide bonds of the antibody in the harvest. That source rises with cell lysis and shear, and so it could rise with the field. A longer culture ends at lower viability and carries more protease into harvest. Viability at the end of culture is a property of the culture and is characterized in PCP-003 and PCR-003, not here.

The A-Mab case study assumes, for simplicity, that harvest has no impact on product quality, and it notes that this might not be true in a real process [@amab2009, p. 85]. PCP-004 keeps the assumption, and the criteria of PCMP-001 Version 2.0 rest on it (@sec-attributes). Three expectations follow for the study:

1. Centrate turbidity falls as the field rises, and host cell protein and DNA in the clarified harvest rise with the field if the shear in the feed zone breaks more cells.
2. Post-clarification turbidity stays low while the depth filter has capacity left, and it rises as the load approaches that capacity.
3. No parameter of the step changes aggregate. Fragments change with the time and temperature of the hold, and with the field only if the field breaks enough cells to reduce the antibody.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-attributes}

@tbl-cqa lists the quality attributes in scope, with the drug substance criterion, the criticality and the Tool #1 score of each. The drug substance CQA register lists every attribute as a CQA. Its level of criticality, from very low (VL) to very high (VH), was assigned with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study as the product of an impact score and an uncertainty score (PCMP-001 §3). PCP-004 placed four of these attributes in scope. Acidic variants enter scope through the hold study only.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cq = cqas_by_keys(["hcp", "residual_dna", "aggregates_hmw", "fragments_lmw", "acidic_variants"]).copy()
_cq["CQA"] = [ALAB[k] for k in ["hcp", "residual_dna", "aggregates_hmw", "fragments_lmw", "acidic_variants"]]
_cq["Category"] = [c[0].upper() + c[1:] for c in _cq["Category"]]
_cq["Tool #1"] = [str(int(x)) for x in _cq["Tool #1"]]
_cq["Acceptance"] = [a + ("^a)^" if q == ALAB["residual_dna"] else "") for a, q in zip(_cq["Acceptance"], _cq["CQA"])]
_cq["CQA"] = [q + ("^b)^" if q == ALAB["acidic_variants"] else "") for q in _cq["CQA"]]
T.frame(_cq[["Category", "CQA", "Acceptance", "Criticality", "Tool #1"]],
        "Quality attributes in scope at harvest, with the drug substance criteria.", "tbl-cqa",
        merge=["Category"], header={"CQA": "Quality attribute", "Acceptance": "Drug substance\ncriterion",
                                    "Tool #1": "Tool #1\nscore"},
        align=["P{2.6cm}", "P{5.0cm}", "P{3.4cm}", "l", "R{1.4cm}"],
        notes=[("a)", f"A dose is {DOSE_MGKG} mg/kg (A-Mab case study) for a reference adult of {DOSE_KG} kg, "
                      f"an assumption of this campaign, so {DOSE_MG:g} mg of antibody."),
               ("b)", "In scope through the hold study S-HAR-HLD only."),
               ("", "The criteria are those of the drug substance CQA register (PCMP-001 Table 3.1). "
                    "Criticality is very low (VL), low (L), moderate (M), high (H) or very high (VH), "
                    "and M-H is moderate to high.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Host cell protein, DNA and aggregate enter harvest in the culture fluid and leave it in the clarified harvest. The step is not credited with clearing any of them. The depth filter media adsorb part of the DNA, but no clearance is claimed for it. The three are in scope because cell breakage in the centrifuge and the filters adds host cell protein and DNA, and because an air-liquid interface can unfold the antibody and add aggregate. Residual DNA has very low criticality. It is measured because DNA fragments and nucleosomes foul depth filters and Protein A resin, so it describes the condition of the feed. Against its drug substance criterion, the DNA clearance credited downstream exceeds what the train must remove by about `{python} n1(DNA_MARGIN)` log10 (@sec-capability).

PCMP-001 Version 2.0 sets no intermediate acceptance criterion for the clarified harvest (PCMP-001 Table 7.1). The derivation of PCMP-001 §7.3 credits harvest with no change in any attribute, so the criteria of the production bioreactor output pass through it unchanged to the load of Protein A capture. For aggregate that criterion is `{python} AGG_C_`. It is the drug substance criterion of ≤ `{python} gn(AGG_DS)` % carried back through three steps. These are the aggregate increase of UF/DF (`{python} n2(AGG_UFDF["predicted_nor_bound95"])` percentage points), the aggregate clearance of cation exchange (`{python} n2(AGG_CEX["predicted_nor_bound95"])`-fold) and the aggregate increase of low-pH viral inactivation (`{python} n2(AGG_VI["predicted_nor_bound95"])` percentage points). All three are values verified for A-Mab at manufacturing scale (PCMP-001 §7.5). PCMP-001 had assumed that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate, and the increase across UF/DF replaces that assumption. The aggregate criterion is stricter than ≤ `{python} n2(agg_row["iac_high_apriori"])` %, the value carried back through the platform worst cases before they were verified for A-Mab. For acidic variants the criterion is `{python} ACID_C_`, the drug substance criterion of `{python} n1(ACID_DS[0])`–`{python} n1(ACID_DS[1])` % carried back through the platform increase of low-pH viral inactivation (`{python} n2(acid_row["downstream_added"])` percentage points). PCR-003 gives the derivation of both and the argument for the change of the aggregate criterion. These criteria rest on the assumption that harvest changes no attribute, and this report uses them to judge the held clarified harvest (@sec-hold).

Fragments have no criterion at harvest or at the production bioreactor. Residual DNA has no intermediate acceptance criterion at any step, because the platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A, so no criterion can be carried back (PCMP-001 §7.3). It is judged on the drug substance only. Version 1.0 applied no criterion to this step.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection {#sec-risk}

The parameters of the study and the study type of each follow the pre-characterization risk assessment RA-001. RA-001 ranked each parameter on its potential to affect a quality attribute and on its potential to interact with another parameter, and it assigned a study type from the combined ranking. It brought `{python} N_PAR` parameters of this step into scope and assigned each of them to univariate study. No parameter was ranked high enough to require a multivariate design, so no screening or response-surface design was run for this step (PCMP-001 §2).

Protein A capture and the two ion exchange steps clear the host cell protein and DNA that cell breakage releases (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). A poorly chosen setting at harvest was therefore expected to load capture more heavily without changing the drug substance.

The range studied extends beyond the NOR at both ends for centrifugation (rcf) and for depth filter load. For post-clarification turbidity the lower edge of the range studied is the lower limit of the NOR, and only the upper edge extends beyond it. A range that stops at the NOR limits cannot show where the operation begins to fail, and an excursion beyond a NOR limit would then have no data behind it.

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

PCP-004 §5.1 planned a scale-down model of the harvest train in three parts, each matched on the quantity that drives its own mechanism. Cell damage in the feed zone was to be reproduced in a bench shear device at the energy dissipation rate calculated for the commercial feed zone. Sedimentation was to be reproduced in a laboratory centrifuge at the relative centrifugal field of the commercial bowl and at a matched ratio of flow to sigma factor. Depth filtration was to be reproduced with disks of the commercial filter media, at the same flux and to the same load per unit area. The plan required the model to be qualified against the commercial train under SOP-1001 before the first characterization run.

No qualification was made (PD-004-03). No laboratory-scale disk-stack centrifuge exists, only a pilot-scale one. The results of the univariate study S-HAR-UNI2 and the hold study S-HAR-HLD are therefore reported at the scale of the study, with no offset to manufacturing scale. The offset of every output is unknown, not zero. PCMP-001 §5 asks a report to state the consequence where the model is not qualified for an output. The consequences for this step are the following:

1. Post-clarification turbidity. The clarification limit of `{python} CLAR_` is judged on results at the scale of the study. The proven acceptable range of depth filter load, which that limit bounds (@sec-par), is therefore a range at the scale of the study, and the capacity of the commercial filter train per unit area may differ. PCP-004 had left this output out of the planned comparison, so its offset would have been unknown even with a qualified model.
2. Centrate turbidity and step yield. No criterion depends on them, and their offsets would only have been recorded (PCMP-001 §7.1).
3. Host cell protein, residual DNA, aggregate and fragments. The conclusions on these attributes are that no parameter changed them within the range studied. An offset that is the same at every level of a series, as a difference or as a ratio, leaves a slope of zero at zero, and the conclusions rest on that. A scale effect that differs between levels would not be seen. PCP-004 §5.1 expected the bench model to under-represent cell lysis, because the acceleration of the feed in the commercial feed zone and the periodic discharge of solids are not fully reproduced. A rise of host cell protein or DNA with the field could therefore be steeper at commercial scale than at the scale of the study.
4. The hold. The changes over the hold are differences within one pool. The level that enters the hold comes from the production bioreactor model at manufacturing scale for aggregate and acidic variants (PCR-003), and from the results of S-HAR-UNI2, at the scale of the study, for fragments (@sec-stats).

The study therefore uses its results to bound ranges and to establish the direction and the approximate size of each effect, as PCP-004 §5.1 intended. It does not predict the concentration of an impurity in a commercial batch.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

PCP-004 §5.2 describes the operation of a characterization run. Each run is a single pass of the whole harvest through the model train, in the order of the commercial operation. The culture is taken from the production bioreactor scale-down model at the end of culture, at the conditions characterized in PCP-003. It is fed to the centrifuge at the field of the run and at the matched ratio of flow to sigma factor. The centrate is collected, sampled and passed over the depth filter train at constant flux to the load of the run, and then over a sterilizing-grade filter. Temperature is held at the commercial set-point throughout, and the time between the end of culture and the end of clarification is held constant. Every parameter not varied in a run is held at its set-point (@tbl-params).

The record of the univariate study S-HAR-UNI2 gives, for each run, the parameter varied, its level and setting, the replicate and the results. It holds none of the records of execution that PCP-004 required (PD-004-07). These are the viability and the cell density of each culture, the order of the runs, the time from the end of culture to clarification and its temperature, the constant flux and the matched ratio of flow to sigma factor, one assay campaign per series with common reagent lots, the calibration status of the equipment for each run, and the agreement of the analysis with Statistics before the first run. The record also does not name the culture of each run, so the analysis by culture that PCP-004 §12 provides for a series run on more than one culture could not be made.

@tbl-sops lists the procedures and the validated methods that govern the study.

```{python}
                 amvs=HARVEST_AMV_REFS + [a for a in AMV_REFS if a[0] == "AMV-3013"]).show()
```

Turbidity by nephelometry (AMV-3015) measured the centrate and the clarified harvest. Host cell protein by ELISA (AMV-3012) and residual DNA by qPCR (AMV-3014) measured the impurity burden of the clarified harvest. Aggregate was measured by SEC-HPLC, validated under `{python} SECM["id"]` (`{python} SECM["sop"]`). The qualified performance of that method is recorded under AMV-3221, with a precision of `{python} gn(SEC_Q["precision_pct"])` % RSD for a single result and a limit of quantitation of `{python} n2(SEC_Q["loq"])` % HMW. Fragments were measured by non-reduced CE-SDS (nrCE-SDS), validated under `{python} CESDS["id"]` (`{python} CESDS["sop"]`), with a repeatability standard deviation of `{python} gn(CESDS["sd_abs"])` percentage points and a limit of quantitation of `{python} n2(CESDS["loq"])` %. In the hold study, charge variants by icIEF (AMV-3013) measured acidic variants. The record names no method for the antibody concentration on which step yield rests, and PCP-004 named none. Host cell protein and DNA are reported per mg of antibody, so they rest on that concentration too. @tbl-responses lists the responses of the two studies with the sample and the method of each, and Appendix C summarizes the recorded performance of the methods.

Fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS on every sample of the univariate study S-HAR-UNI2 and the hold study S-HAR-HLD, and neither study has a fragment result by SEC. PCMP-001 §7.8 sets nrCE-SDS as the method for fragments at every step from `{python} AMD["id"]`, because host cell protein co-elutes with the low molecular weight species in SEC and raises the fragment result. That bias grows with the host cell protein present, and a clarified harvest carries more host cell protein than any later intermediate.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

PCP-004 §5.4 planned four sample points in every run. They were the unclarified culture before the feed to the centrifuge starts, the centrate, the filtrate after depth filtration and the clarified harvest after sterilizing-grade filtration (PCP-004 Appendix B). The unclarified culture was to be the reference against which impurity release and any change in the size variants are judged.

The record of the univariate study S-HAR-UNI2 holds results for the clarified harvest and the turbidity of the centrate. It holds no result for the unclarified culture or for the filtrate after depth filtration, and no host cell protein or DNA result for the centrate, because these samples were not scheduled in the study record (PD-004-04). The comparison within a run that the impurity release criterion and the product quality criterion of PCP-004 §7 describe can therefore not be made, and @sec-stats states how those criteria were applied instead. In the turbidity series the centrate turbidity is not reported, because the material of each level was prepared by adding centrate (@sec-univariate).

Each level was run in duplicate, so each setting has two results for each response that its series measured. The set-point condition appears in the centrifugation (rcf) and the depth filter load series, which gives `{python} N_SPR` runs at which every parameter was at its set-point and the clarified harvest was not adjusted.

In the hold study S-HAR-HLD one pool of clarified harvest was divided between two storage temperatures, `{python} COLD` and `{python} WARM`, and sampled on days `{python} join_and(DAYS)`. Each sample was tested for aggregate by SEC, fragments by nrCE-SDS and acidic variants by icIEF.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

Each response of the univariate study S-HAR-UNI2 was analysed against the setting of the parameter varied in its series, by linear regression on the `{python} N_PER` runs of the series. PCP-004 §5.4 and §5.5 name the replicates at the set-point condition as the estimate of the variation between runs against which every effect is tested. The `{python} N_SPR` runs with every parameter at set-point give that estimate on `{python} DF_SP` degrees of freedom, and the slopes are tested, and their intervals calculated, against it. The slope was tested at α = `{python} ALPHA`, the significance level of the campaign (PCMP-001 §6.2). A response is affected by a parameter when its slope is significant at that level. Each regression is reported with its R² and its residual standard deviation, as PCP-004 §5.5 requires. No threshold is set for either, and no decision rests on them.

With the residual error of the regression, on `{python} DF_RES` degrees of freedom, in place of the set-point replicates, the same slopes are significant and no other. The intervals change with the error term, and Appendix B gives the residual version as a sensitivity.

Each change is reported over the whole range studied, as the slope times the width of the range, with its 95 % confidence interval. Where no slope was detected, the interval gives the precision of the comparison, which is the range of changes across the range studied that the data do not exclude. For a significant slope PCP-004 §5.5 asks for the change across the NOR, compared with the precision of the method, and for an effect smaller than the method can resolve to be reported as detected and not material. PCP-004 sets no size for the smallest difference a method tells apart (PD-004-08). This report takes it as the repeatability limit, the difference that two single results exceed by chance with a probability of 5 %. That is `{python} n2(Z_RES)` times the standard deviation of a single result, at the mean of the set-point runs. At α = `{python} ALPHA`, about one test in twenty of a response with no real effect gives a significant slope by chance (PCMP-001 §6.2). The study made `{python} N_TESTS` such tests, apart from the check of the turbidity challenge (@sec-res-turbidity).

PCP-004 §5.5 allows a quadratic term where the relationship is not linear, and it names no test for curvature. None was fitted. Where the individual results show a response that is not linear, as for post-clarification turbidity against depth filter load, the report describes them, and the decision rests on the individual results against the limit. The variation between the set-point replicates does not include such a departure from a straight line, so for a response that is not linear the interval of the slope understates its uncertainty. Every result of turbidity, host cell protein and DNA lies above the limit of quantitation of its method, so no result was excluded.

The impurity release criterion of PCP-004 §7 compares host cell protein and DNA in the clarified harvest with the same measurement on the unclarified culture of the run, and the product quality criterion compares aggregate before and after the step. The samples those comparisons need were not taken. This report therefore judges both criteria on the slope against the setting, the analysis PCP-004 §5.5 sets for every response. A parameter passes them over its range where no slope is detected for host cell protein, residual DNA or aggregate. PCP-004 lists fragments in scope but names them neither as a response of its study nor in its criteria, and they are judged the same way.

No response-surface model is fitted for this step, and no Monte Carlo propagation of a fitted model is made (PCP-004 §5.5). A range from this study holds with the other parameters at their set-points. The capability of the drug substance comes from a Monte Carlo simulation of the whole train through the step models (PCMP-001 §6.5). It simulates `{python} cn(NMC)` batches, each parameter drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of one sixth of the width of its NOR, and clipped to the range studied.

PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §5 judges a held pool against the criteria it must meet on entering the next step. For aggregate and acidic variants the criteria for the load of Protein A capture are those of the production bioreactor output, which pass through harvest unchanged (@sec-attributes). PCMP-001 sets no fragments criterion for that load. This report compares fragments with the drug substance criterion of `{python} FRAG_C_`, and no fragments criterion of the train is stricter (PCMP-001 Table 7.1). Two rules of the judgement are this report's own, chosen after the results of the hold study S-HAR-HLD were known. They set the level that enters the hold and the change over it.

1. The level that enters the hold is the highest level expected in routine manufacture, and the lowest for the lower limit of acidic variants. For aggregate and acidic variants it is the end of the two-sided 95 % prediction interval of a single batch over the NOR of the production bioreactor, at manufacturing scale (PCR-003). Each end is a one-sided 97.5 % limit. For fragments, which the bioreactor designs did not measure, it is the highest result of S-HAR-UNI2. PCP-004 provides culture from the set-point of the production bioreactor for those runs (§5.2 and §12), and their fragments match the process model at the end of a culture at set-point (@sec-res-attributes). A longer culture within its NOR ends at lower viability and carries more fragments into harvest (@sec-platform), and no result of the campaign measures that increase. The fragments level that enters the hold is therefore not the highest level expected in routine manufacture.
2. The change over the hold is the largest change from day `{python} DAYS[0]` at each temperature. That is the largest increase, and for the lower limit of acidic variants the largest decrease. The expected level after the hold is the level that enters plus that change, and it meets the criterion or it does not. A change smaller than the difference between the two results of the pool on day `{python} DAYS[0]` is not taken as resolved.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params gives the parameters of the step with their set-points, NORs, ranges studied and classes. The set-points and the NORs are those against which the study was planned. None was changed at Version 2.0.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_pp = pd.DataFrame([[NAME[k] + ("^a)^" if k == "turbidity" else ""), UNIT[k], fg(P[k].setpoint),
                     f"{fg(P[k].nor[0])}–{fg(P[k].nor[1])}", f"{fg(P[k].prange[0])}–{fg(P[k].prange[1])}",
                     CLS[k]] for k in KEYS],
                   columns=["Parameter", "Unit", "Set-point", "NOR", "Range studied", "Class"])
T.frame(_pp, "Parameters of harvest and clarification, each studied one factor at a time.", "tbl-params",
        align=["P{4.4cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "l"],
        notes=[("a)", "Measured, not set. Its range is the range of turbidity presented to capture.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The ranges serve different purposes. Centrifugation (rcf) runs from `{python} RLO_["centrifuge_g"]` to `{python} RHI_["centrifuge_g"]`, so that it covers the lower fields, at which clarification is less complete, and the higher fields, at which more cells may break. Depth filter load runs to `{python} RHI_["depth_filter_load"]`, beyond the upper NOR limit of `{python} NORHI_["depth_filter_load"]` and past the load at which the media are expected to approach capacity. Post-clarification turbidity is the response of the other two parameters, so its range is the range of turbidity presented to capture, not a range of settings dialled in at the centrifuge. The range studied of each parameter is its knowledge space, and no proven acceptable range is claimed beyond it.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

S-HAR-UNI, the univariate study of Version 1.0, ran from `{python} WIN[UNI1]`. Version 1.0 described it and narrated its outcome, but gave no result for any parameter effect, and it has no data in the record. Its two study events are reported in @sec-events.

S-HAR-UNI2 was made from `{python} WIN[UNI2]` to give the harvest parameters recorded results (PD-004-01). Each parameter was run at `{python} NLEV` levels (`{python} join_and(LEVNAMES)`) in duplicate, with the other parameters at their set-points. That gives `{python} N_RUNS` runs in three series of `{python} N_SER`. S-HAR-UNI2 also measured fragments, which PCP-004 does not name as a response of its study.

@tbl-levels compares the levels of S-HAR-UNI2 with those of PCP-004 Appendix A. For depth filter load they are the same. For centrifugation (rcf) the two inner levels, `{python} pv("centrifuge_g", EXTRA["centrifuge_g"][0])` and `{python} pv("centrifuge_g", EXTRA["centrifuge_g"][1])`, lie outside the NOR of `{python} NOR_["centrifuge_g"]`. For post-clarification turbidity the levels of `{python} pv("turbidity", EXTRA["turbidity"][0])` and `{python} pv("turbidity", EXTRA["turbidity"][1])` were run in place of the upper NOR limit of `{python} NORHI_["turbidity"]` that the plan named. Of the NOR limits, `{python} NOTRUN_TXT` were therefore not run as levels. In both series the NOR lies between levels that were run, so the ranges of @sec-par still cover it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_pos = ["Lower edge of range studied", "Lower limit of NOR", "Set-point", "Upper limit of NOR",
        "Upper edge of range studied"]
_lr = []
for k in KEYS:
    for i in range(NLEV):
        _pl = fg(PLAN_LEV[k][i])
        if k == "turbidity" and i == 1:
            _pl += "^a)^"
        _lr.append([f"{NAME[k]}, {UNIT[k]}", _pos[i], _pl, LEVNAMES[i], fg(LEV[k][i])])
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_lr, columns=["Parameter", "Level in PCP-004", "PCP-004", "Level in S-HAR-UNI2",
                                   "S-HAR-UNI2"]),
        "Levels planned in PCP-004 Appendix A and levels run in S-HAR-UNI2.", "tbl-levels",
        merge=["Parameter"], header={"PCP-004": "Setting,\nPCP-004", "S-HAR-UNI2": "Setting,\nS-HAR-UNI2"},
        align=["P{3.4cm}", "P{4.2cm}", "R{1.7cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "R{2.3cm}"],
        notes=[("a)", "The lower edge of the range studied and the lower limit of the NOR coincide, so the "
                      "plan has four distinct levels for this parameter.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Three elements of the planned design were not run. The depth filter load series was run once, on centrate from the set-point field, and the turbidity series on material from it (PD-004-06). PCP-004 planned the depth filter load series on centrate from `{python} RLO_["centrifuge_g"]` and from `{python} RHI_["centrifuge_g"]`, after the centrifugation series, to bracket the interaction between the two parameters, and the turbidity material from both (PCP-004 §5.5 and §6.2). The range of depth filter load in @sec-par therefore holds for centrate produced at the set-point field. The turbidity series was not loaded onto a scale-down Protein A column, and the pressure that the filter train develops was not measured (PD-004-05). The column pressure and the cycle yield of the Protein A load challenge (PCP-004 §6.2) therefore have no result.

In the turbidity series the clarified filtrate was adjusted to each level with centrate, the turbidity of each preparation was measured, and the attributes were recorded. This is the preparation PCP-004 §6.2 describes, a blend of clarified harvest and retained centrate. Material prepared this way carries the particle size distribution of the centrate it was made from, which is not the distribution that a depth filter at the end of its capacity would pass. The turbidity range of @sec-par is therefore a range of turbidity delivered to capture, and no claim is made about the material that a filter near capacity passes (PCP-004 §12).

## Hold study of the clarified harvest {#sec-hold-design}

The hold study S-HAR-HLD was made from `{python} WIN[HLD]` (PD-004-02). PCP-004 placed the hold of the clarified harvest outside its scope (PCP-004 §1), and Version 1.0 of the plan did not foresee a hold study. One pool of clarified harvest, made at the set-point of the step, was held at `{python} COLD` and at `{python} WARM` for `{python} HOLD_D` days and sampled as @sec-sampling describes. The record does not name the culture from which the pool was made.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Set-point reproducibility {#sec-reproducibility}

@tbl-reproducibility gives the `{python} N_SPR` runs with every parameter at set-point and the scatter of the duplicates at every level. The duplicates of turbidity, host cell protein and DNA scattered by about the precision of their methods, with pooled relative standard deviations of `{python} n1(POOL["clarified_turbidity_ntu"][0])`, `{python} n1(POOL["hcp_out_ng_mg"][0])` and `{python} n1(POOL["dna_out_pg_mg"][0])` % against `{python} n1(METH["AMV-3015"]["precision_pct"])`, `{python} n1(METH["AMV-3012"]["precision_pct"])` and `{python} n1(METH["AMV-3014"]["precision_pct"])` % for a single result of the method. Aggregate and fragments also scattered at about method precision. Their pooled duplicates gave `{python} n1(POOL["aggregate_out_pct"][0])` % RSD against `{python} gn(SEC_Q["precision_pct"])` % for SEC, and a standard deviation of `{python} n3(FRAG_POOL_SD)` against `{python} gn(CESDS["sd_abs"])` percentage points for nrCE-SDS. Assay variation is therefore most of the variation between runs of these responses. Residual DNA had the widest scatter among the set-point runs, `{python} n1(SPCV["dna_out_pg_mg"])` % RSD, from `{python} sig3(DNA_SPR[0])` to `{python} sig3(DNA_SPR[1])` pg/mg.

## Centrifugation (rcf) {#sec-res-rcf}

@tbl-clarification gives the turbidity results of the centrifugation (rcf) and depth filter load series at each level, and @fig-turbidity plots them. @tbl-regression gives every regression of the study, and Appendix A every individual result.

Centrate turbidity fell as the field rose, from a mean of `{python} n1(CEN[lo_g])` NTU at `{python} RLO_["centrifuge_g"]` to `{python} n1(CEN[sp_g])` NTU at the set-point and `{python} n1(CEN[hi_g])` NTU at `{python} RHI_["centrifuge_g"]`. Most of the fall lay below the set-point. Of the fall of `{python} n1(CEN_FALL1)` NTU across the range, `{python} n0(100 * CEN_FRAC)` % took place between `{python} RLO_["centrifuge_g"]` and `{python} SP_["centrifuge_g"]`. The slope across the range was `{python} rr("centrifuge_g", "centrate_turbidity_ntu")` NTU (95 % confidence interval `{python} ci("centrifuge_g", "centrate_turbidity_ntu")` NTU, `{python} pR("centrifuge_g", "centrate_turbidity_ntu")`). The results do not fall on a straight line. They level off above the set-point. Across the NOR of `{python} NOR_["centrifuge_g"]` the slope gives a change of `{python} n1(PS_CEN["chg"])` NTU. The repeatability limit of the turbidity method at the mean of the set-point runs is `{python} n2(PS_CEN["res"])` NTU, so the change is material.

Post-clarification turbidity fell slightly with the field, by `{python} n2(-REG[("centrifuge_g", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")]["chg"])` NTU across the range (95 % confidence interval `{python} ci("centrifuge_g", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")` NTU, `{python} pR("centrifuge_g", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")`). Across the NOR the slope gives a change of `{python} n2(PS_CRCF["chg"])` NTU, smaller than the repeatability limit of `{python} n2(PS_CRCF["res"])` NTU. The effect is therefore detected and not material. The highest result was `{python} n2(MAX_CLAR_RCF)` NTU, at `{python} pv("centrifuge_g", MAX_CLAR_RCF_AT)`, so every level met the clarification limit of `{python} CLAR_`.

No slope was detected for host cell protein, residual DNA, aggregate, fragments or step yield. Host cell protein came closest, with a change of `{python} rr("centrifuge_g", "hcp_out_ng_mg")` ng/mg across the range (95 % confidence interval `{python} ci("centrifuge_g", "hcp_out_ng_mg")` ng/mg, `{python} pR("centrifuge_g", "hcp_out_ng_mg")`). The interval includes no change, and its point estimate is a fall, not the rise that more cell breakage at a higher field would give.

