## Depth filter load {#sec-res-dfl}

Post-clarification turbidity stayed between `{python} n2(DFL_LOW_RANGE[0])` and `{python} n2(DFL_LOW_RANGE[1])` NTU from `{python} RLO_["depth_filter_load"]` to `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", LOW3_DFL[-1])`. Both results at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", PREV_DFL)`, `{python} n2(PREVR[0])` and `{python} n2(PREVR[1])` NTU, were higher than every result at the lower loads, and both lay below the limit. Both results at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)`, `{python} T.num(TOPR[0])` and `{python} T.num(TOPR[1])` NTU, exceeded the clarification limit of `{python} CLAR_`. Depth filter load therefore failed the clarification criterion at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)` and met it at every lower level.

The linear slope across the range, `{python} rr("depth_filter_load", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")` NTU (95 % confidence interval `{python} ci("depth_filter_load", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")` NTU, `{python} pR("depth_filter_load", "clarified_turbidity_ntu")`), describes these results poorly, because nearly all of the change lies between the two highest levels, and its interval leaves that departure from a straight line out (@sec-stats). Across the NOR of `{python} NOR_["depth_filter_load"]` the slope gives a change of `{python} n2(PS_CDFL["chg"])` NTU, and the level means changed by `{python} n2(DFL_NOR_MEAN_CHG)` NTU. Both exceed the repeatability limit of `{python} n2(PS_CDFL["res"])` NTU, so the effect is material. The decision on the range rests on the individual results against the limit.

No slope was detected for centrate turbidity (`{python} pR("depth_filter_load", "centrate_turbidity_ntu")`), as expected, because the centrate is made before the filter and the whole series used centrate from one field. No slope was detected for host cell protein, residual DNA, aggregate, fragments or step yield. The depth filter media adsorb part of the DNA, and the share they take up could change with the load (PCP-004 §4.3). The change in residual DNA across the range was `{python} rr("depth_filter_load", "dna_out_pg_mg")` pg/mg (95 % confidence interval `{python} ci("depth_filter_load", "dna_out_pg_mg")` pg/mg, `{python} pR("depth_filter_load", "dna_out_pg_mg")`). The study therefore gives no evidence of such a change, at the precision of the qPCR and of the runs.

## Post-clarification turbidity {#sec-res-turbidity}

The measured turbidity of the prepared material tracked its target, with a slope of `{python} n2(REG[CHECK]["slope"])` NTU per NTU of target and an R² of `{python} n3(REG[CHECK]["r2"])`. The preparation therefore gave the challenge levels intended, from `{python} n2(TURB_MEAS[0])` to `{python} T.num(TURB_MEAS[1])` NTU.

No slope was detected for host cell protein, residual DNA, aggregate, fragments or step yield across `{python} RNG_["turbidity"]`. Step yield came closest, with a change of `{python} rr("turbidity", "step_yield_pct")` percentage points across the range (95 % confidence interval `{python} ci("turbidity", "step_yield_pct")`, `{python} pR("turbidity", "step_yield_pct")`). No difference in these attributes of the material presented to capture was therefore detected across its turbidity. The effect on capture itself, which the mechanism expects through fouling of the Protein A bed, was not measured, because the Protein A load challenge was not run (@sec-univariate).

## Quality attributes across the three series {#sec-res-attributes}

Across the three series no slope was detected for any quality attribute at α = `{python} ALPHA`. The 95 % confidence intervals of @tbl-regression give the precision of these comparisons. The widest interval end reached `{python} n0(CI_REL["hcp_out_ng_mg"])` % of the set-point mean for host cell protein, `{python} n0(CI_REL["dna_out_pg_mg"])` % for residual DNA, `{python} n0(CI_REL["aggregate_out_pct"])` % for aggregate and `{python} n0(CI_REL["lmw_cesds_pct"])` % for fragments. The data do not exclude a change of up to that size across a range. The comparison is least precise for residual DNA, whose method and runs scatter most (@sec-reproducibility).

Across all `{python} N_RUNS` runs, aggregate ranged from `{python} n2(BAND["aggregate_out_pct"][0])` to `{python} n2(BAND["aggregate_out_pct"][1])` %, well below `{python} AGG_C_`, the aggregate criterion of the production bioreactor output, which passes through harvest unchanged. Fragments ranged from `{python} n2(BAND["lmw_cesds_pct"][0])` to `{python} n2(BAND["lmw_cesds_pct"][1])` %, below the drug substance criterion of `{python} FRAG_C_`. Host cell protein and residual DNA have no criterion at harvest, so their results are reported for information and are neither met nor not met. Acidic variants were not measured in S-HAR-UNI2, and no range of this report is supported for them. The `{python} N_SPR` set-point runs of S-HAR-UNI2 averaged `{python} n2(FRAG_SP)` % fragments, and the process model at set-point carries `{python} n2h(FRAG_NOM["bioreactor"])` % at the end of culture. @fig-attributes plots every attribute result against the setting of its series.

These results keep the A-Mab assumption that harvest has no impact on product quality [@amab2009]. Turbidity responded to the parameters, and no effect on the attributes was detected within the ranges studied, at the precision of the runs. The support has three limits. The study measured the attributes in the clarified harvest only, so the change across the step, against the culture before harvest, was not measured. The criteria of the production bioreactor output pass through harvest unchanged (@sec-attributes), and that use assumes the step itself changes no attribute. Each parameter was varied with the others at their set-points, so no combination of two parameters away from their set-points is covered. The results are also at the scale of the study (@sec-sdm).

```{python}
        _m = _g.groupby("value")[_rk].mean()
        _ax.plot(_m.index, _m.values, color=C1, lw=1.0, zorder=2)
        _ax.scatter(_g["value"], _g[_rk], s=14, color=C1, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
        _ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.5)
        _ax.set_axisbelow(True)
        _ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(THOU)
        if _rk in ("hcp_out_ng_mg", "dna_out_pg_mg"):
            _ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(THOU)
        if _r == len(ATTRS) - 1:
            _ax.set_xlabel(f"{NAME[_pk]} ({UNIT[_pk]})")
        if _c == 0:
            _ax.set_ylabel(RLAB[_rk])
    _lo = float(U[_rk].min())
    _hi = float(U[_rk].max())
    _axs[_r, 0].set_ylim(0, _hi * 1.25)
_fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

At `{python} WARM` all three attributes rose over the `{python} HOLD_D` days. Fragments rose at every time point, from `{python} n2(HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", WARM)]["d0"])` % on day `{python} DAYS[0]` to `{python} n2(HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", WARM)]["vals"][-1])` % on day `{python} HOLD_D`, by `{python} n2(HC[("lmw_cesds_pct", WARM)]["end"])` percentage points. Acidic variants rose by `{python} n2(HC[("acidic_pct", WARM)]["end"])` percentage points, all of it after day `{python} DAYS[1]`, and aggregate by `{python} n2(HC[("hmw_pct", WARM)]["end"])`.

On day `{python} HC[("hmw_pct", COLD)]["inc_day"]` aggregate was `{python} n2(HC[("hmw_pct", COLD)]["inc"])` percentage points above its result on day `{python} DAYS[0]`, and on day `{python} HOLD_D` it was back at that level. Acidic variants stayed within `{python} n2(ACID_COLD_MAX)` percentage points of their result on day `{python} DAYS[0]`, which is less than the standard deviation of a single icIEF result at that level, `{python} n2(ICIEF_SD)` points. ## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mechanism}

Centrate turbidity followed the sedimentation mechanism of @sec-platform. A higher field raises the settling velocity of cells and debris, so more of them reach a disc and are captured before the fluid leaves the stack. The fall levelled off above the set-point. That is consistent with a remaining turbidity carried by particles too small to settle in the time available at any field studied. The study did not measure particle size.

No rise in host cell protein or DNA was detected at the higher fields. The shear in the feed zone rises with the speed of the bowl, and cells broken there would add both to the centrate. At the scale of the study the data show no such rise up to `{python} RHI_["centrifuge_g"]`. The model was not qualified, and PCP-004 §5.1 expected a bench model to under-represent lysis, so this result does not show that a commercial feed zone breaks no cells at the highest field.

Post-clarification turbidity fell a little as the field rose, and the centrate results show why. A higher field passed less turbidity to the depth filter, which then had less fine material to pass. The second effect the mechanism allows, finer debris from broken cells, was not seen, which agrees with the absence of a detected rise in host cell protein and DNA.

Post-clarification turbidity against depth filter load showed the capacity of the media. Up to `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", LOW3_DFL[-1])` the filter retained the fine material of the centrate as well as at the lowest load. At `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", PREV_DFL)` both results were a little higher, and at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)` the mean turbidity rose `{python} n1(DFL_TOP_RATIO)`-fold and crossed the limit. This is the shape the mechanism predicts for media that approach saturation, in which retained solids fill the void space and occupy the charged sites until fine material passes. The study places the onset of the rise between `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", PREV_DFL)` and `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)` for centrate made at the set-point field. Centrate from a lower field carries more turbidity (@sec-res-rcf) and is expected to saturate the media at a lower load. The bracket that PCP-004 planned in order to measure this was not run.

No effect of a parameter on fragments in the clarified harvest was detected. Across the range of centrifugation (rcf) fragments changed by `{python} rr("centrifuge_g", "lmw_cesds_pct")` percentage points (95 % confidence interval `{python} ci("centrifuge_g", "lmw_cesds_pct")`, `{python} pR("centrifuge_g", "lmw_cesds_pct")`), so the data show no dependence on the field at that precision. Disulfide reduction after cell lysis would make fragments rise with the field (@sec-platform), and the data did not show it within the range studied. The hold study showed that fragments depend on temperature, as clipping by proteases predicts. Acidic variants followed the same pattern, because deamidation also runs faster at a higher temperature. For the operation of the step this means that the field and the filter load change how much fine material reaches capture. While the clarified harvest is held, proteases keep clipping the antibody and deamidation keeps forming acidic variants, and both run faster when it is warmer. The time and the temperature of the hold therefore change how far fragments and acidic variants rise before capture.

# Design space {#sec-design-space}

No design space is claimed for this step. A design space is a multivariate region, and no multivariate design was run here (PCP-004 §8). Each proven acceptable range of @sec-par holds with the other parameters at their set-points, and no combination of two parameters away from their set-points is claimed. One interaction is expected on mechanistic grounds. A lower field passes more solids to the depth filter and would bring the capacity of the media forward, so the range of depth filter load holds for centrate produced at the set-point field. Operation outside a NOR and inside the proven acceptable range is supported by this study for the attributes it measured, and a planned change is assessed under change control [@ichq10].

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

PCP-004 §7 sets four decision criteria. They are those of Version 1.0, in its words, and no result of the studies was used to set or change them. Their application to the univariate study S-HAR-UNI2 is the following:

1. Impurity release. Host cell protein and residual DNA in the clarified harvest are compared with the same measurements on the unclarified culture that produced it. A level passes when no increase is detected at α = `{python} ALPHA`, or when a detected increase is smaller than the method can resolve. With no result for the unclarified culture, a parameter passes over its range where no slope against the setting is detected for either impurity (@sec-stats).
2. Clarification. Post-clarification turbidity is compared with the upper limit of its NOR, `{python} CLAR_`. The criterion asks whether a harvest setting delivers clarified harvest within the NOR. A setting that delivers more has not clarified to the NOR, whatever the impurity results show, and that is why the proven acceptable range of depth filter load stops at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", PAR["depth_filter_load"][1])`. The basis of `{python} CLAR_` is the NOR itself, which is set from production experience. It is not derived from a measured effect on Protein A capture. The criterion was applied to each result of the centrifugation (rcf) and depth filter load series. In the turbidity series the turbidity is the challenge level itself, so the criterion does not apply there.
3. Product quality. Aggregate is compared before and after the step, and a level passes when no increase is detected at α = `{python} ALPHA`. With no result before the step, a parameter passes over its range where no slope against the setting is detected for aggregate. Fragments were judged the same way.
4. Step yield is reported and not gated. It is given for every level in Appendix A and compared with the set-point runs. Every result lay between `{python} n1(BAND["step_yield_pct"][0])` and `{python} n1(BAND["step_yield_pct"][1])` %, against a mean of `{python} n1(YIELD_SP)` % for the set-point runs, and no slope against the setting was detected for it in any series.

A parameter meets the criteria over a range when every level in that range passes the first three. The proven acceptable range is then that range, bounded at the levels tested. Where a level fails, the range is bounded at the last level that passed (PCP-004 §7 and §8).

PCP-004 §8 left four rules to this report (PD-004-08). A size for the smallest difference a method tells apart in the impurity release criterion is not needed, because no slope was detected for host cell protein or DNA. No threshold is applied to the R² or the residual standard deviation of a regression, because no decision rests on them. For post-clarification turbidity, whose series is a challenge, the range is decided by the impurity release and product quality criteria alone. A rule to combine two depth filter load series, on centrate from `{python} RLO_["centrifuge_g"]` and from `{python} RHI_["centrifuge_g"]`, is not needed, because only one series was run. @tbl-par gives the result for each parameter.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows_par = []
for pk in KEYS:
    rng, nor, par = (f"{fg(P[pk].prange[0])}–{fg(P[pk].prange[1])}", f"{fg(P[pk].nor[0])}–{fg(P[pk].nor[1])}",
                     f"{fg(PAR[pk][0])}–{fg(PAR[pk][1])}")
    mg = " / ".join("none" if m == 0 else fg(m) for m in MARG[pk])
    ca = CLOSEST[pk]
    _rows_par.append([f"{NAME[pk]}, {UNIT[pk]}", rng, nor, "Impurity release and product quality, by slope",
                  f"{ANAME[ca][0].upper() + ANAME[ca][1:]}, {pp(REG[(pk, ca)]['p_sp'])}", par, mg])
    if pk == "turbidity":
        _rows_par.append([f"{NAME[pk]}, {UNIT[pk]}", rng, nor, "Clarification", "not applicable^a)^", par, mg])
    elif pk == "centrifuge_g":
        _rows_par.append([f"{NAME[pk]}, {UNIT[pk]}", rng, nor, f"Clarification, ≤ {fg(CLAR_LIM)} NTU",
                      f"Highest {n2(MAX_CLAR_RCF)} NTU, at {pv(pk, MAX_CLAR_RCF_AT)}", par, mg])
    else:
        _rows_par.append([f"{NAME[pk]}, {UNIT[pk]}", rng, nor, f"Clarification, ≤ {fg(CLAR_LIM)} NTU",
                      f"{T.num(TOPR[0])} and {T.num(TOPR[1])} NTU at {pv(pk, TOP_DFL)}, not met", par, mg])
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_rows_par, columns=["Parameter", "Range studied", "NOR", "Criterion", "Closest", "PAR",
                                     "Margin"]),
        "Proven acceptable range of each parameter, with the criterion that decides it.", "tbl-par",
        merge=["Parameter", "Range studied", "NOR", "PAR", "Margin"],
        header={"Range studied": "Range\nstudied", "Closest": "Result closest\nto the criterion",
                "Margin": "Margin to the\nNOR, below /\nabove"},
        align=["P{2.4cm}", "R{1.5cm}", "R{1.5cm}", "P{2.7cm}", "P{3.7cm}", "R{1.5cm}", "R{1.9cm}"], style="rows",
        notes=[("a)", "The turbidity of the series is the challenge level itself."),
               ("", f"p-values of the slope against the setting, tested on the variation between the {N_SPR} runs "
                    f"with every parameter at set-point ({DF_SP} degrees of freedom), the error term of the "
                    "regressions of the Results. Each range holds with the other parameters at their set-points "
                    "and is stated at the scale of the study.")],
        notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

Centrifugation (rcf) met the clarification criterion at every level, and no slope was detected in its series for the impurities or for aggregate. Its proven acceptable range is the whole range studied, `{python} PAR_["centrifuge_g"]`, and the NOR of `{python} NOR_["centrifuge_g"]` lies inside it with `{python} pv("centrifuge_g", MARG["centrifuge_g"][0])` of margin at each end.

Depth filter load failed the clarification criterion at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)`. Its proven acceptable range is bounded at the last level that passed and runs from `{python} RLO_["depth_filter_load"]` to `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", PAR["depth_filter_load"][1])`. The upper limit of the NOR coincides with that edge. A NOR limit on the edge of the proven range leaves no margin for the ordinary variability of the commercial operation (PCP-004 §8). The lower limit of the NOR lies `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", MARG["depth_filter_load"][0])` inside the range.

PCP-004 §7 asks for a failure to be investigated before the range is reported, and the record holds no investigation beyond the results themselves. Both runs at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)` exceeded the limit, and their two results, `{python} T.num(TOPR[0])` and `{python} T.num(TOPR[1])` NTU, differ by less than the repeatability limit of the turbidity method. The response rose steeply between the two highest levels, as the saturation of the media predicts (@sec-mechanism). The failure is therefore taken as the capacity of the media and not as an error of the runs.

Post-clarification turbidity met the impurity release and product quality criteria over the whole range studied. Its proven acceptable range, `{python} PAR_["turbidity"]`, answers a different question from the clarification criterion. It is the range over which the turbidity challenge showed no effect on the attributes measured in the clarified harvest. It does not cover the performance of Protein A capture, because the load challenge was not made (PD-004-05). A harvest setting must still deliver clarified harvest within the NOR of `{python} NOR_["turbidity"]`, and every batch is monitored against that NOR (@sec-control). The lower limit of the NOR is the lower edge of the range studied, so the two coincide there. The upper limit of the NOR lies `{python} pv("turbidity", MARG["turbidity"][1])` inside the range.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

This study gives no capability for the outputs of harvest. It has no model of the step from which batches could be simulated, and its results are at the scale of the study. The capability of the drug substance comes from the Monte Carlo simulation of the whole train described in @sec-stats. @tbl-capability gives it for the attributes that PCP-004 placed in scope.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cq2_cap = cqas_by_keys(CAPK).set_index(pd.Index(CAPK))
_dec_cap = {"fragments_lmw": 3, "hcp": 1, "residual_dna": 6, "aggregates_hmw": 3}
_rows_cap = []
for k in CAPK:
    m, s = float(MC[k].mean()), float(MC[k].std(ddof=1))
    _rows_cap.append([ALAB[k], _cq2_cap.loc[k, "Criticality"], _cq2_cap.loc[k, "Acceptance"],
                  f"{m:.{_dec_cap[k]}f}", f"{s:.{_dec_cap[k]}f}", f"{float(CAPT.loc[k, 'Cpk']):.2f}",
                  "yes" if CAPT.loc[k, "Cpk"] >= CPK_TARGET else "no",
                  f"{int(POOS.loc[k, 'n_oos'])} of {int(POOS.loc[k, 'n']):,}"])
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_rows_cap, columns=["Attribute", "Criticality", "Criterion", "Mean", "SD", "Cpk", "Target",
                                     "Outside"]),
        "Capability of the drug substance in the simulation of the train, for the attributes in scope of PCP-004.",
        "tbl-capability",
        header={"Criterion": "Drug substance\ncriterion", "Target": f"Cpk ≥\n{CPK_TARGET}",
                "Outside": "Simulated\nbatches\noutside"},
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "l", "P{2.6cm}", "R{1.5cm}", "R{1.5cm}", "r", "l", "R{1.6cm}"],
        notes=[("", f"Mean and SD of {N_MC:,} simulated batches, in the unit of the criterion. The target Cpk is "
                    "that of PCMP-001 §7.9.")],
        notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

Every Cpk lies above the target of `{python} CPK_TARGET` that PCMP-001 §7.9 sets for a CQA in routine manufacture, and so above its minimum of `{python} CPK_MIN`. No simulated batch fell outside any of these criteria. With none of `{python} cn(N_MC)` batches outside, the one-sided 95 % upper bound of the probability of an out of specification batch is `{python} n2(100 * UB0)` %. That bound covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the step models. The attributes are judged at harvest on their individual results (@sec-res-attributes) and, for the held pool, by the approach of @sec-stats.

Fragments are the attribute that the register assigns to harvest. Their drug substance Cpk is `{python} n2(CPK_FRAG)`, from a simulated mean of `{python} n2(MC_FRAG)` % against the criterion of `{python} FRAG_C_`. The process model at set-point carries `{python} n2h(FRAG_NOM["bioreactor"])` % fragments at the end of culture and `{python} n2h(FRAG_NOM["ufdf"])` % in the drug substance. Its level at the end of culture agrees with the set-point runs of S-HAR-UNI2 (@sec-res-attributes).

Residual DNA is controlled by clearance, not by a release test [@amab2009, p. 47]. The set-point runs of S-HAR-UNI2 carried a mean of `{python} sig3(DNA_SP)` pg DNA per mg of antibody. For a dose of `{python} gn(DOSE_MG)` mg of antibody (`{python} DOSE_MGKG` mg/kg for a `{python} DOSE_KG` kg adult, a body weight assumed by this campaign) that is `{python} sig3(DNA_DOSE)` ng per dose. The drug substance criterion is ≤ `{python} gn(DNA_DS)` ng per dose, so the purification train must remove about `{python} n1(DNA_LOG_NEEDED)` log10 of DNA. The step models credit Protein A capture, cation exchange and anion exchange with `{python} gn(DNA_LRV["protein_a"])`, `{python} gn(DNA_LRV["cex"])` and `{python} gn(DNA_LRV["aex"])` log10 of DNA clearance. These clearances are inputs that the configuration of the process model sets, not results of this study. The reports of those steps give the DNA results of their designs (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). Host cell protein and aggregate depend in the same way on the purification steps that clear them.

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the rule of PCMP-001 §7.7. A parameter that affects a CQA is a CPP or a WC-CPP, and the two differ in the risk that the parameter falls outside its acceptable range in operation. A parameter that affects process performance and no CQA is a KPP, and one that affects neither is a GPP. An attribute is affected by a parameter when the effect is significant at α = `{python} ALPHA` (PCMP-001 §6.2). Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for a practically relevant effect, so each class below states the size of each effect across the proven acceptable range and the margin of that range to the NOR. The size of an effect is the difference between the level means at the two ends of the range.

- Centrifugation (rcf) was classified as a `{python} CLS["centrifuge_g"]`. It changed the clarity of the feed to capture. Across its proven acceptable range of `{python} PAR_["centrifuge_g"]` centrate turbidity changed by `{python} n1(PARCHG_CEN1)` NTU and post-clarification turbidity by `{python} n2(PARCHG_CRCF)` NTU, with every result below the clarification limit. Across the NOR the change in post-clarification turbidity is smaller than the repeatability limit of the turbidity method (@sec-res-rcf). No effect on a quality attribute or on step yield was detected, and the confidence intervals of @tbl-regression bound what the study could have missed. The margin of the range to the NOR is `{python} pv("centrifuge_g", MARG["centrifuge_g"][0])` at each end. The class rests on host cell protein, residual DNA, aggregate and fragments in the clarified harvest, the attributes the study measured.
- Depth filter load was classified as a `{python} CLS["depth_filter_load"]`. It changed post-clarification turbidity by `{python} n2(PARCHG_CDFL)` NTU across its proven acceptable range of `{python} PAR_["depth_filter_load"]`, where every result lay between `{python} n2(DFL_LOW_RANGE[0])` and `{python} n2(PREVR[1])` NTU, and the turbidity exceeded the clarification limit at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)`. No effect on a quality attribute or on step yield was detected. The margin of the range to the NOR is `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", MARG["depth_filter_load"][0])` below and none above. The upper limit of its NOR lies on the edge of that range at the scale of an unqualified model, and the turbidity of the clarified harvest, tested on every batch, is the control that detects a filter that approaches its capacity (@sec-control).
- Post-clarification turbidity was classified as a `{python} CLS["turbidity"]`. It is measured, not set. This class is a judgement. Its basis is that over `{python} PAR_["turbidity"]` no effect on a quality attribute of the clarified harvest or on step yield was detected. The margin of its proven acceptable range to the NOR is none at the lower end, where both meet the edge of the range studied, and `{python} pv("turbidity", MARG["turbidity"][1])` at the upper end. By the rule above a GPP also has no effect on process performance, and the data do not show that for turbidity. The mechanism expects turbidity to affect Protein A capture through fouling of the bed, and that effect was not measured, because the Protein A load challenge was not run (PD-004-05).

No effect of a parameter of this step on a CQA was detected within the range studied, so the step has no CPP and no WC-CPP. This agrees with the A-Mab assumption that harvest has no impact on product quality.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

The control strategy of the drug substance has two purposes. Product quality and safety are assured by controlling the parameters linked to a CQA within the limits of the design space, and process consistency by controlling the KPPs within established limits and monitoring the process attributes [@amab2009]. Harvest contributes to the second. Its contributions are the following:

1. Centrifugation (rcf) and depth filter load are controlled within their NORs, `{python} NOR_["centrifuge_g"]` and `{python} NOR_["depth_filter_load"]`, as KPPs.
2. The turbidity of the clarified harvest is measured on every batch by nephelometry (AMV-3015) as an in-process control (PCP-004 §4.1 and §8), against its NOR of `{python} NOR_["turbidity"]`. The upper limit of that NOR is the clarification limit. The control detects a centrifuge that clarifies poorly or a depth filter near its capacity. PCP-004 §5.3 makes it the measurement by which the clarified harvest is released to capture. The upper NOR limit of depth filter load lies on the edge of its proven acceptable range, so this test is the control that detects an excursion of the filter load.
3. No quality attribute is controlled at harvest. Host cell protein and DNA are controlled by their clearance at Protein A capture, cation exchange and anion exchange (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008), and residual DNA by that clearance, not by a release test [@amab2009]. Fragments have no criterion at harvest. They are judged at the downstream steps against the criteria of PCMP-001 Table 7.1 and tested at release of the drug substance by nrCE-SDS.
4. The hold of the clarified harvest is not a parameter of PCP-004, and this report sets no limit for it. On one pool, the hold study supports a hold of up to `{python} HOLD_D` days at `{python} COLD` or at `{python} WARM` for aggregate, fragments and the upper limit of acidic variants, the attributes it measured. The fragment level taken to enter the hold is not the highest expected in routine manufacture (@sec-stats). Bioburden and endotoxin were not part of the hold study, so a hold time in manufacturing needs that support as well. A cold hold slows the rise of fragments and acidic variants.

PCR-003 sets the monitoring of acidic variants at harvest of every production batch, with an action limit of `{python} n2(AM["action_limit"])` %, as part of the mitigation of the acidic-variant risk it accepted. The hold study shows that acidic variants rise in a clarified harvest held at `{python} WARM`, by `{python} n2(HC[("acidic_pct", WARM)]["end"])` percentage points in `{python} HOLD_D` days, so the time and the temperature of a sample before it is tested bear on that monitoring.

These contributions roll up into PCMR-001, which consolidates the control strategy of the train. The ranges and classes are those against which the `{python} N_PPQ` process performance qualification batches planned in PTP-001 will be run at the receiving site.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The harvest train of A-Mab behaves as the platform mechanisms predict. Settling velocity rises with the centrifugal field, so less turbidity reaches the depth filter at a higher field, and most of that fall lies below the set-point. The depth filter keeps its clarity until its load approaches the capacity of the media, which for centrate from the set-point field lies between `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", PREV_DFL)` and `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)` at the scale of the study. No effect of either parameter, or of the turbidity of the clarified harvest within `{python} RNG_["turbidity"]`, on a quality attribute was detected. Fragments and acidic variants change with the time and the temperature of the hold, not with the operation of the step.

Confidence in the scale-down model is the main limitation. The model was not qualified, so no output has a known offset from manufacturing scale, and the results give directions and approximate sizes, not commercial levels. Two consequences matter most. The capacity of the commercial depth filter train per unit area may differ from that of the study. With the upper NOR limit of depth filter load on the edge of its proven acceptable range, a lower capacity at commercial scale would place that limit beyond the edge, and the turbidity test on every batch is the control that would detect it. Cell breakage at the highest field may also be greater in the commercial feed zone than in the study, so the absence of a rise in host cell protein and DNA holds at the scale of the study. Protein A capture and the two ion exchange steps clear what such breakage would add.

The results rest on two studies that PCP-004 did not plan. Every parameter result comes from the univariate study made during the re-analysis (PD-004-01), not from the planned study. The hold judgement comes from the `{python} HOLD_D`-day hold study (PD-004-02), by rules for the entering level and the change that this report chose after the results were known (@sec-stats). The univariate study also departed from the design of PCP-004 (PD-004-04 to PD-004-07). The culture before harvest, the filter pressure and the Protein A load challenge were not measured, the depth filter load series was not run on centrate from both ends of the range of centrifugation (rcf), three NOR limits were not run as levels, and the records of execution were not kept. Where the plan left a rule open, such as the smallest difference a method must tell apart, this report states the rule it applied (PD-004-08).

In routine manufacture the turbidity test on every batch detects poor clarification, and the purification steps clear host cell protein and DNA. The process performance qualification batches at the receiving site will run the step at commercial scale within its NORs (PTP-001).

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. Turbidity responded to the parameters of harvest, and no effect on a quality attribute was detected. No slope was detected for host cell protein, residual DNA, aggregate, fragments or step yield in any series, at α = `{python} ALPHA`. The A-Mab assumption that harvest has no impact on product quality is kept, for the attributes measured in the clarified harvest.
2. The proven acceptable ranges are `{python} PAR_["centrifuge_g"]` for centrifugation (rcf), `{python} PAR_["depth_filter_load"]` for depth filter load and `{python} PAR_["turbidity"]` for post-clarification turbidity, at the scale of the study and with the other parameters at their set-points. Each NOR lies inside its range. The upper NOR limit of depth filter load lies on the edge of its range.
3. Centrifugation (rcf) and depth filter load are KPPs, and post-clarification turbidity is a GPP. The step has no CPP and no WC-CPP.
4. Held for `{python} HOLD_D` days at `{python} COLD` or `{python} WARM`, the clarified harvest meets the criteria for the load of Protein A capture for aggregate and fragments and the upper limit for acidic variants. It was judged by rules chosen after the results were known (@sec-stats), on one pool and for the attributes measured. The lower limit for acidic variants is not met at the level that enters the hold, which PCR-003 reports.
5. In the simulation of the train, the drug substance Cpk for fragments, the attribute the register assigns to harvest, is `{python} n2(CPK_FRAG)`, above the target of `{python} CPK_TARGET`.
6. The scale-down model was not qualified, and every result is stated at the scale of the study.
7. The two study events of Version 1.0, a depth filter flush turbidity above its alert limit and a post-clarification turbidity above the NOR on one run, have no bearing on these conclusions.

# Study events and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-record}

PCP-004 calls a change made during execution that is not a revision of the plan a deviation (PCP-004 §13). A process characterization study is not GMP manufacture, so this report raises no deviation. It records the events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded as study events, under the numbers Version 1.0 gave them, and the departures from PCP-004 as discrepancies from the plan.

## Study events {#sec-events}

Version 1.0 recorded `{python} N_EV` study events, both in S-HAR-UNI. @tbl-events lists them with the outcome Version 1.0 recorded. S-HAR-UNI has no data in the record and no result of it enters this report, so neither event bears on a conclusion.

### DEV-004-01, depth filter flush turbidity above its alert limit

During the pre-use flush of a depth filter of lot LOT-DF-4408, the turbidity of the flush was `{python} gn(dev_004_01_flush_turbidity_ntu)` NTU, above the alert limit of the flush. The investigation found the initial flush volume insufficient. The lot was within its expiry date, `{python} lot_df_4408_expiry`. Version 1.0 retained the run in the analysis of S-HAR-UNI.

### DEV-004-02, post-clarification turbidity above the NOR on one run

In-process turbidity monitoring (AMV-3015) found a post-clarification turbidity above the NOR on one run, with a highest value of `{python} gn(dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu)` NTU against the upper NOR limit of `{python} CLAR_`. The investigation found loading of the depth filter near its maximum as the cause. Version 1.0 retained the run in the analysis of S-HAR-UNI. The event is of the same kind as the result of S-HAR-UNI2 at `{python} pv("depth_filter_load", TOP_DFL)`, where both runs exceeded the limit (@sec-res-dfl).

## Discrepancies from the plan {#sec-discrepancies}

The record holds `{python} N_PD` departures from PCP-004 as discrepancies from the plan (@tbl-discrepancies).

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(discrepancy_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Discrepancies from PCP-004. {#tbl-discrepancies}")
```

PD-004-01. PCP-004 planned a univariate study of each harvest parameter, S-HAR-UNI, which Version 1.0 described and narrated without a result for any parameter effect. S-HAR-UNI2 was made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, from `{python} WIN[UNI2]`, to give the harvest parameters the recorded results that Version 1.0 lacked. Each parameter was run at `{python} NLEV` levels in duplicate with the others at set-point, and post-clarification turbidity as a challenge. Its levels leave out three NOR limits, `{python} NOTRUN_TXT`, and it measured fragments, which PCP-004 does not name as a response of its study (@sec-univariate).

PD-004-02. No plan foresaw a hold study. S-HAR-HLD held the clarified harvest at two temperatures for `{python} HOLD_D` days, from `{python} WIN[HLD]`, with aggregate by SEC, acidic variants by icIEF and fragments by nrCE-SDS at every time point. It was made because Version 2.0 judges a held intermediate against its intermediate acceptance criteria and Version 1.0 had no hold result to judge. The rules for the level that enters the hold and for the change over it were chosen after the results were known (@sec-stats), and the judgement of @sec-hold carries that limitation.

PD-004-03. PCP-004 required the scale-down model to be qualified against the commercial train before the first characterization run. No qualification was made, because no laboratory-scale disk-stack centrifuge exists, only a pilot-scale one. Every result is therefore reported at the scale of the study, with no offset to manufacturing scale, and @sec-sdm states the consequence for each output.

PD-004-04. PCP-004 planned samples of the unclarified culture, the centrate and the depth filtrate for host cell protein and DNA, so that the impurity release and product quality criteria compare each run with its own culture (PCP-004 §5.4 and Appendix B). Only the clarified harvest was sampled, because the samples before and after the step were not scheduled in the study record. The comparison within a run could not be made, and the report judges both criteria on the slope of each result against its parameter (@sec-stats). The study therefore shows whether a parameter changed an attribute of the clarified harvest, not whether the step changed it.

PD-004-05. PCP-004 planned to record the pressure that the filter train develops (objective 3 and §5.1) and a Protein A load challenge with column pressure and cycle yield (§6.2). Neither was measured, because neither was scheduled in the study record. Objective 3 is met for the particulate content of the clarified harvest only, and the effect of turbidity on capture is not known (@sec-res-turbidity).

PD-004-06. PCP-004 planned the depth filter load series on centrate from `{python} RLO_["centrifuge_g"]` and from `{python} RHI_["centrifuge_g"]`, run after the centrifugation series, and the turbidity material made from both (§5.5, §6.2, §11 and Appendix A). One series was run on centrate from the set-point, and the turbidity series on material from it. The record gives no reason. The interaction between the two parameters is therefore not bracketed, and the range of depth filter load holds for centrate from the set-point field (@sec-design-space).

PD-004-07. PCP-004 required records of the execution of each run (§5.2, §5.3, §6.2, §9, §10 and §12), and @sec-operation lists them. None of them is in the record, and the record gives no reason. The conditions under which each run was made can therefore not be confirmed from the record beyond its setting.

PD-004-08. PCP-004 §8 leaves four rules to this report. They are the smallest difference a method must tell apart, the use of the fit statistics, the decision on the range of post-clarification turbidity and the combination of two depth filter load series. The report states and applies each (@sec-stats and @sec-par). It also judges the impurity release and product quality criteria on the slope of each result, because the samples those criteria need were not taken (PD-004-04).
